Can you believe it? I went 15-0 with my straight-up picks last week. I guess it was an easy week, like some said. As for my picks against the spread, it wasn't quite as good, but it was better than it's been. I went 9-6 for the week, which I will take. The season marks are now 59-74-3 ATS and 87-48-1 straight up. Let's see if we can get perfect against the spread this week. Yeah, right. I will take three games above. 500 again as I make the climb to respectability. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Washington Commanders at New York Giants (-2.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime The Giants are back home after beating the Eagles and now face a Commanders team that probably has to win this to have any chance at the playoffs. The Giants' defense has been dominant up front as of late, and that will continue here as they contain Jayden Daniels . Giants keep winning. Pick: Giants 23, Commanders 14 New England Patriots at Detroit Lions (-2.5) Munich on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is a big game for both teams, but especially so for the Patriots after they got blown out by the Packers at home last week. The Lions won at Miami and didn't play great, but they will get it going on offense here. New England is struggling on defense, so look for the Lions to win it with a strong offensive showing. Pick: Lions 30, Patriots 24 Kansas City Chiefs (-3.5) at Atlanta Falcons Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs snapped a two-game losing streak last week in beating the Jets , while the Falcons were blown out in Madrid by the Bengals . The defense had some major issues in that game. That will be the same here after the trade of safety Jessie Bates. Chiefs stack another victory. Pick: Chiefs 23, Falcons 17 Houston Texans at Cleveland Browns (+4.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is a big game for both teams in terms of the playoff picture. The Texans looked dominant against the Chargers last week, but this is a second straight road game. It won't matter. Their defensive front will dominate whoever plays quarterback for the Browns . But the Cleveland defense will keep them in it. Pick: Texans 21, Browns 20 Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) The Packers are coming off an impressive road victory over the Patriots and Jordan Love has been on fire. But the Minnesota defense is special and now they have Kirk Cousins to play quarterback. Even so, look for the Packers to win another one as their defense limits Cousins and the offense. Pick: Packers 27, Vikings 17 Jacksonville Jaguars (-10.5) at Tennessee Titans The Titans are coming off a bye, while the Jaguars are coming off a victory last Thursday at Baltimore. They will be rested too. Jacksonville is riding high as one of the top teams in the league and made some moves at the trade deadline to get even better. Though this is a rivalry, with some unpredictable games, this won't be. Jaguars big. Pick: Jaguars 31, Titans 17 Miami Dolphins (+3.5) at Indianapolis Colts This is the dog game of the week between two struggling teams. But one is young and playing hard on the way up, while one is on the way down after trading away assets. The problem for Miami is that quarterback Malik Willis is out. That means Kyle McCord will start at quarterback. Miami will hang around against the depleted Colts team, but the Colts will win it late. Pick: Colts 23, Dolphins 22 Carolina Panthers at New Orleans Saints (-2.5) This is an enormous game in the division, even though both teams have just three victories. The winner will be in first place. The Saints beat the Browns last week, while the Panthers have lost three straight. The Saints make it four in a row as Tyler Shough has a big day. Pick: Saints 24, Panthers 21 Buffalo Bills (-8.5) at New York Jets The Bills are coming off a hard-fought road victory at Minnesota. The turnaround will be tough, but they are playing at a high level. The defense is improving. Look for Josh Allen to carve up the Jets' defense. Pick: Bills 34, Jets 21 Seattle Seahawks (-6.5) at Las Vegas Raiders Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Seahawks will start Drew Lock at quarterback again in this one. He was just OK last week against Arizona. But the Raiders have big-time defensive issues. For the Raiders, it's Fernando Mendoza time after they traded Kirk Cousins to Minnesota. This is a tough defense for a first NFL start. Look for Lock to win it as the Seahawks' defense does the rest. Pick: Seahawks 24, Raiders 16 Los Angeles Rams at Arizona Cardinals (+9.5) The Rams lost at home to the Cardinals a few weeks ago and now must play without Puka Nacua . How will they move the ball? The Cardinals will start rookie Carson Beck at quarterback. Going against Myles Garrett and company can be a problem. Rams win it, but it's low-scoring. Pick: Rams 19, Cardinals 16 San Francisco 49ers at Dallas Cowboys (+4.5) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys can't afford another loss in their division race, so this is a huge game for them. The 49ers are riding high and that offense will challenge the Dallas defense. But I think the Dallas offense will be even better. Upset special. Dak Prescott has a bigger day than Brock Purdy . Pick: Cowboys 30, 49ers 28 Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals (-3.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is for first place in the division. The Bengals are riding high behind their passing game and Joe Burrow . But the defense can't stop the run. The Steelers will run it here to keep Burrow off the field. It doesn't work. The Bengals will once again win it behind Burrow and the passing game. Pick: Bengals 27, Steelers 21 Los Angeles Chargers (+4.5) at Baltimore Ravens Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This game had promise before the season, but the Ravens are without Lamar Jackson and the Chargers are 0-8. Jacoby Brissett will start for the Ravens, which should help the offense some. The Chargers have struggled on offense, but I think their defense will keep them in this. It's close. New York (5-2-1) has a three-game lead over Washington in the NFC East, but the Dallas Cowboys (4-5) at least have a shot to catch the Giants this season. So, who is favored to win on Thursday? The latest odds continue to move in favor of the Giants, who are expected to have J.J. McCarthy (hip pointer) under center in this game. New York has shifted all the way up to -142 to win , as 62 percent of the moneyline bets and 69 percent of the spread bets at DraftKings are on Harbaugh's team. He’s targeting New York as a home favorite to cover: I may have included the New York Giants in last week's edition of my Fraud Rankings , but my biggest issue with them has been their strength of schedule. Will I be betting on them when they take on teams like the Jaguars and 49ers in the coming weeks? Likely not, but they once again have a game against a bad team on Thursday Night Football when they face the Washington Commanders, and much like the majority of the season, I expect them to take care of business against an inferior opponent. These two teams played to a tie in Week 5 earlier this season, but with it being a road game for the Giants and the fact that they had Jameis Winston at quarterback, I think we can admit they're in a better spot in the rematch. J.J. McCarthy has been surprisingly solid to begin his tenure with the Giants, ranking fifth in the NFL in completion percentage over expected (+5.3%) amongst quarterbacks who have played 60+ snaps this season. It's also no coincidence that over the last three weeks, the Giants have led the league in net yards per play at +1.5. Meanwhile, the Commanders continue to be a poorly coached team that doesn't thrive in any area, ranking in the bottom half of the NFL in virtually every metric. Washington is coming off a 20-13 home loss to the Los Angeles Rams, while the Giants are coming off a 19-11 road win against the Philadelphia Eagles. The Commanders are averaging 21.5 points per game with a points-per-game differential of -3.75. The Giants have fared a little better, averaging 22.8 points per game with a 1.25-point-per-game differential. Just one of their wins (Week 4 vs. Arizona) has been by 10 points or more, which means the Giants have squeaked by so far. The good news for the Giants is their defense has been dominant. New York has allowed just 172 points to opponents this season, the seventh-lowest mark in the league, making a valid argument that the defense has carried the team for most of the season. What will this week bring? Let’s take a look. Another Divisional Win? Please. The Giants have not beaten Washington since 2023. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Giants erased the 13-year losing streak in Philadelphia on Sunday. This week, they have a chance to erase a five-game streak in which they haven’t defeated the Commanders, home or away. The Giants erased the 13-year losing streak in Philadelphia on Sunday. This week, they have a chance to erase a five-game streak in which they haven’t defeated the Commanders, home or away. The Giants and Commanders, of course, tied in their meeting earlier this year. Before that, the last time the Giants beat Washington was November 19, 2023. So they are long overdue. With a win, the Giants would improve to 3-0-1 in the division and remain a couple of steps ahead of the Dallas Cowboys, who seem hot on their heels in the NFC East race. So yes, a lot is at stake for the Giants, who are 1-6 in games played on Thursday night since 2020. The Giants are aiming for their second straight win on Thursday Night Football . New York Giants general manager Joe Schoen has been working the phones to try to get John Harbaugh additional reinforcements. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A short workweek is challenging enough, but throw in the trade deadline, and it gets even more complicated. A short workweek is challenging enough, but throw in the trade deadline, and it gets even more complicated. The Giants have been heavily linked to Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. Still, as of Sunday, Jay Glazer of Fox Sports reported that New York withdrew its offer after the Colts said they wanted much more for their lead back. That doesn’t mean that things can’t change, but it’s hard to see a deal happening, considering the Giants don’t have a 2027 fourth- or fifth-round pick to include in a trade, which appears to be a requisite to get a deal done. Given that the Colts also reportedly want a second-round pick, it’s hard to envision the Giants caving, especially after head coach John Harbaugh acknowledged the team isn’t one player away. And then there is the other side of the coin, which is defensive tackle. The Giants really haven’t been strongly linked to any defensive tackles, at least not in the way they’ve been linked to Taylor. Could a surprise move be coming? Harbaugh, in fact, expressed optimism that Skattebo and McCarthy, whose injuries appear to be the most significant, will be available for Thursday night. Jameis Winston briefly entered the Week 9 contest in relief of McCarthy Getty Images The New York Giants appear to have survived another injury scare at the quarterback position. J.J. McCarthy returned to Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles after spending time in the sideline medical tent and locker room while being evaluated for a hip injury. McCarthy took a hard hit to his lower abdomen on a quarterback keeper in the third quarter. Eagles linebacker Zack Baun led with his helmet while attempting to stop McCarthy's run and made contact with McCarthy's side on the tackle. McCarthy attempted to throw on the sideline before heading to the locker room and was in obvious pain after he completed his throwing motion. He grabbed at his side and fell to the turf as medical staff came to his assistance. Despite the clear discomfort, he was able to get back into game action just before the end of the quarter. J.J. McCarthy is in pain after an apparent injury. 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/qP3JfP2PUn The Giants were mostly quiet on offense during McCarthy's Week 9 start and scored only six points before he left with the injury. McCarthy was 9-for-13 for 101 passing yards and ran three times for another 11 yards ahead of his brief exit. Although it seems that McCarthy will remain in action beyond this week, if the injury acts up on him and forces him to miss time, his potential absence may be a significant blow to the NFC East-leading Giants. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights John Breech predicts every Week 10 game, including a Lions victory over the Patriots in Munich Imagn Images I just got back from the NFL game in Spain, and I think I should probably start going more often, since Week 10 ended up being my best week of the year for picks. I went 14-1 straight up, and yes, I should probably just retire at this point, but I don't want to retire while I'm on top; I want to retire when I hit rock bottom, which might actually happen this week. Speaking of rock bottom, I went to McDonald's four times while I was in Spain, and let me just say, I only went there because Madrid had the nicest McDonald's I've ever seen. I mean, just look at this place. I'm now starting to understand why those Falcons players went to McDonald's. This is like the nicest McDonald's I've ever seen in my life. Wouldn't put it past Madrid to have a Michelin rated McDonald's #Bengals #Falcons #Spain https://t.co/w8WixT6iN2 pic.twitter.com/TMAeeXm9Fk There were also people tailgating inside of a Taco Bell. Taco Bell is in fact a mad house. NFL fans everywhere. Nothing like a pregame cheesy gordita crunch. #Bengals #Falcons #Spain #Madrid https://t.co/0uAafegmaM pic.twitter.com/cpjfyWy33X If you need just one reason to ever visit Spain, tailgating at Taco Bell has to be it. Unfortunately, there's no game in Spain this week, so there will be no tailgating at Taco Bell, but there is a game in Germany, and it will be the final NFL game of this year that kicks off at 9:30 a.m. ET, which is definitely for the best, because I've reached my maximum limit for 9:30 a.m. ET games. The Patriots and Lions will be playing in the early game on Sunday. So who's going to win? Let's get to the Week 10 picks and find out. Alright, now let's get to the picks for real NFL Week 10 picks Commanders (2-5-1) at Giants (5-2-1) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. ET (Amazon Prime) Based on everything I've seen from the Commanders , I already know exactly how this game is going to play out: Washington is going to keep this thing close until the end only to lose (or tie) because no one in the organization has any idea what to do in any key late-game situation. For instance, let's go back to Week 5 when the Commanders pulled off one of the all-time worst late-game gaffes in a tie with the Giants . Washington had the game won. All Jayden Daniels had to do was literally anything except what he actually did. The Commanders can't get the play off in time and this game ends in a tie pic.twitter.com/WmPp6q5hU0 Look at the Giants players in that clip. They're celebrating. When the other team is CELEBRATING a tie, that means you lost. Surely Daniels and the Commanders learned their lesson, right? Wrong. In their Week 9 game against the Rams , they needed a 32-yard touchdown on the final play, but instead of throwing it in the end zone, Daniels threw the ball five yards past the line of scrimmage because the Commanders apparently thought they were going to be able to lateral the ball to each other all the way into the end zone. There's a reason that never works. With the game on the line Jayden Daniels can’t get the ball out of his hand. pic.twitter.com/2D8I1YWsiA Now, you could blame Daniels for this stuff, but ultimately, it falls on the coaching staff. In the Rams' game, Daniels said he was just running the play that was called . In the Giants' game, someone on the coaching staff should have made it clear to everyone on the field that the clock has to come to a stop on that play, whether it's a spike or a player running out of bounds. So what does this mean for this game? It means that the Commanders are actually playing decent football and if their coaching staff doesn't let them down, I think they have a good chance of winning. The Giants are beat up at quarterback, they're beat up at running back, and they're surviving by the skin of their teeth. Four of their five wins have come by one score. Good teams win close games -- are you taking notes, Commanders -- and I'm starting to feel like the Giants might be a sneaky good team. To me, this is arguably the most fascinating game of Week 10. If the Commanders lose, their season is all but over, but if they win, they'll be right back in the NFC East race. I feel like this is a pick I'm going to regret as soon as I make it, but I'm taking the desperate Commanders. PICK: Commanders 24-17 over Giants Patriots (5-4) vs. Lions (6-2) in Munich Sunday, 9:30 a.m. (NFL Network) With this game being played in Munich, I feel like this would be the perfect time to answer the one question that has been on all of our minds over the past few months: Who would win a beer-chugging contest between Mike Vrabel and Dan Campbell? With these two guys heading to the beer capital of the world, there's no reason not to find out. And to be honest, based on how the Patriots have been playing recently, Vrabel could probably use a few beers right about now. I'm not in charge of scheduling events for the NFL in Germany this week, which is probably for the best, but if I were, I would rent out the Hofbrauhaus and then give both Campbell and Vrabel one full stein of beer to chug. Instead of a coin toss on Sunday, this is how we would decide who's getting the ball first. I was at the Hofbrauhaus once and it took me an hour to finish my beer. The Germans were definitely laughing at me. What's the record for most beers drank in one sitting here? I think I'm going to try to break it. pic.twitter.com/UQ5kOtxyPL The Germans might be laughing at the Patriots, too, if they can't turn things around this week. Vrabel is known as one of the smartest defensive-minded coaches in the NFL, but he hasn't figured out how to stop any NFC North teams. The Patriots have faced two NFC North teams this year and not only have they gone 0-2, but they're surrendering an average of 37.5 points per game. Yikes. The NFC North is so good that I might not pick against any of their teams for the rest of the season unless they're playing another NFC North team. If you've looked at the NFL standings at any point over the past 24 hours, you may have noticed that the NFC North is arguably the best all-around division in the NFL this year and possibly ever. All four teams are at least three games over .500, which is the first time that's ever happened through the first nine weeks. Oh, and did I mention that the NFC North is 20-4 against all other divisions. They are destroying everyone. On the other hand, you have the Patriots, who are 3-1 against AFC East opponents, but 2-3 against everyone else. The Patriots have had one of the worst passing defenses in the NFL over the past several weeks, and now, they have to face off against a QB in Jared Goff who ranks in the top five in passing yards per game this year. The Lions might put up 50 points. The good news for the Patriots is that even if the Lions do put up a 50-burger, New England might still keep up. Detroit has given up the MOST passing yards per game this year (260.9), so Drake Maye could certainly get some turkey carving practice for Thanksgiving here by carving up the Lions' defense. That being said, I've decided not to trust Maye against good teams. The Patriots have faced six opponents this year with winning records, and in those games, Maye has thrown 11 interceptions to nine touchdowns. Based on how I think this game is going to go, Vrabel might need a Hofbrauhaus beer after it's over. PICK: Lions 34-27 over Patriots Texans (3-5) at Browns (5-4) Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (Fox) Deshaun Watson did not play in Week 9 for the Browns , but there's no chance he's going to miss this game. This is the ultimate revenge, though, I can't say for sure whether this is more about the Texans trying to get revenge on him or he's trying to get revenge on the Texans. Actually, now that I'm thinking about it, there might not be any revenge involved at all here. Since trading Watson to the Browns in March 2022, the Texans have made the playoffs three times, and they've won their division twice. On the other hand, Watson has been injured for the majority of his time in Cleveland; he's won just 14 games since 2022, and the Browns have paid him roughly $14.5 million per win. If Tom Brady had earned $14.5 million per win, he would have made over $3 billion in his career. Do you know how many Hofbrauhaus beers you could buy with that money? The worst part for the Browns is that they're still in QB purgatory, which is basically where they've been since returning to the NFL in 1999. Although Watson is playing well this year, especially late in games, I'm not sure that's a good thing. If he somehow leads Cleveland to the playoffs, the Browns might actually talk themselves into re-signing him, which doesn't seem like a great idea. The New England Patriots have had a tough time locking down elite offenses, giving up a pile of points to Green Bay, Jacksonville, Chicago, and Buffalo already this season. The Pats' blitz-centric schemes aren't getting the pressure they need to hide what has become a problem in the pass defense. New England entered Week 9's matchup with the Packers allowing far too many big plays through the air and were absolutely exposed, with Jordan Love striking for almost 400 yards. They won't, however, stay in the country: their game against the Detroit Lions will take place in Munich, Germany. Perhaps unsurprisingly given their 45-27 defeat to the Packers, FanDuel Sportsbook has the Patriots listed as underdogs for that game. Odds for Patriots vs. Lions in NFL Week 10 Spread: Lions -2.5 Moneyline: Patriots +124 | Lions -146 Over/under: 50.5 The Patriots and Lions are projected to face off in a high-scoring game on Sunday. The over/under of 50.5 is tied for the highest among all New England games so far this year, and a hurdle the two teams should be capable of clearing. That said, while the Patriots have hit the over in six straight games, the Lions have not. In fact, they have not hit the projected mark three contests in a row. Obviously, there are a multiple factors that go into a game being a high- or low-scoring affair. That being said, if New England's offense and defense perform like they did against Green Bay, the scoring potential will — for better or worse — be immense on both sides of the ball. That game marked the Patriots last shutout and the 31st shutout in team history. Detroit entered the 2022 game with the top ranked offense, averaging an NFL-high 35 points per game and 437 yards per game. They were held to 0 points and 312 total yards. Detroit had scored at least 24 points and rushed for at least 130 yards in each of their first four games that season, and the Lions were held to 0 points and 101 rushing yards by the Patriots. It was the second straight time the Lions traveled to New England with a top ranked unit. When the Lions played at Gillette Stadium on Nov. 23, 2014, the Patriots rolled to a 34-9 win against the Lions' top ranked defense. Detroit remains one of six teams that the Patriots have never lost to at Gillette Stadium. Detroit is 0-3 in their three games played at Gillette Stadium. The Patriots lead the all-time series by an 8-5 margin but are 3-3 on the road against Detroit with a 1-2 record at the Pontiac Silverdome and a 2-1 record at Ford Field. This week will be played in Munich, Germany as a Detroit home game. potential shootout in Munich, Germany, between the Detroit Lions (6-2) and New England Patriots (5-4)! Detroit is tied for the second-longest winning streak (4) behind Denver (5), while New England is coming off a loss and has dropped two of the past three games. New England is coming off one of its worst performances of the season, but in my opinion, it was the worst. Christian Gonzalez and the New England secondary were torched by Jordan Love and the Packers for 372 passing yards and three touchdowns. Without Josh Jacobs, Green Bay was able to average 4.0 yards per carry on New England, and Christian Watson (7/171/1) and Matthew Golden 10/164/1) got whatever they wanted through the air. Offensively, Drake Maye had his worst outing in an up-and-down season. Maye kicked off the year with seven picks through four games and had one interception over the next four games before tossing three against the Packers last week for an NFL-high 11 interceptions. New England’s running game doesn’t look good as both Rhamondre Stevenson (doubtful) and TreVeyon Henderson (questionable) are injured, plus AJ Brown , so Maye has to continue chucking and carrying this offense. Detroit is coming off four-straight wins over Arizona (45-21), Green Bay (20-17), Minnesota (19-15), and Miami (19-9). The Lions defense has turned it around lately, holding all four opponents to 21 or fewer and 15.5 points per game during the winning streak. The Lions rank third in sacks (27), with three different players recording at least five, which is what Detroit is relying on due to the explosive plays allowed in the pass game. While Detroit has limited the big plays during the winning streak, the Lions have still allowed an NFL-high of 34 pass plays of 20-plus yards. If AJ Brown returns for New England, I’d expect Maye and Brown to warm up with some short yardage passes to gain a rhythm before taking some shots. Detroit’s offense will likely do the same after 50 total passes in the last two games and fewer than 200 passing yards for Jared Goff , which is something he hasn’t done since 2024. He had three interceptions that could have been five or six, and season-lows in completion percentage (55.3%) and rushing yards (3). away.headline: Patriots vs. Lions Wednesday injury report: AJ Brown returns, three ruled out
away.blurb: Wide receiver A.J. Brown was on hand for it. After missing back-to-back weeks due to a knee issue in addition to the high ankle sprain that sent him to injured reserve in September, the former All-Pro returned as a limited participant to begin Detroit Lions prep. But running back TreVeyon Henderson, offensive lineman Ben Brown and cornerback Carlton Davis III stayed among the sidelined in Foxborough and have officially been ruled out for the matchup in Munich. RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness — out) CB Carlton Davis III (knee — out) An illness that kept Henderson hospitalized for multiple days will now keep the running back out for a third straight game. The Patriots will be without another Brown on offense after the team’s starting left guard exited last Sunday’s 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers with a knee injury. And in the secondary, a knee injury will also keep Davis from taking the field in Munich after he’d worked back from a neck injury throughout October. That leaves four non-participants from Wednesday potentially in play for the NFL international series. FB Reggie Gilliam (knee — IR return) G Greg Van Roten (hamstring — IR return) S Kerby Joseph (knee — PUP return) But a pair of 21-day practice windows are now open for New England along with one 53-man roster spot. After Van Roten headed back to practice last week, Gilliam did so to start work on the Lions. The fullback spent the past five games on injured reserve. He marks the fifth IR return designation utilized by New England. NFL rules allot eight per club. The New England Patriots held practice inside Gillette Stadium on Wednesday before taking an evening flight overseas. Here’s the first injury report ahead of Sunday’s 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff at Allianz Arena. “There’s going to be guys that go to Germany that won’t play,” head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters prior to practice. No. 1 was among seven partial participants for the Patriots on Wednesday. The June trade acquisition hadn’t practiced since late last month and has missed six games altogether amid a season featuring nine receptions for 101 yards. RB Jacob Saylors (neck, hamstring) Under center, Maye continued to be a full participant for New England while carrying a listing due to his right shoulder. The reigning AFC Offensive Player of the Month completed 55 percent of his passes for 299 yards with three touchdowns and three interceptions last weekend. Prior to the blowout loss at home, the quarterback had turned the calendar to November by totaling three scores and only four incompletions in an AFC East comeback against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium.

Stevenson is reportedly dealing with a plantaris tendon issue in the back of his knee. He won't need surgery, according to Rapoport. The 28-year-old exited New England's Week 9 loss to the Green Bay Packers early. He has 102 carries for 399 yards and two touchdowns this season. His absence is another blow to the Patriots, who are already without second-year running back TreVeyon Henderson. Henderson, who hasn't played since Week 7, revealed last week that he suffered an "unexpected and unusual medical emergency" that hospitalized him for several days. New England's running back injuries leave Corey Kiner and Lan Larison as the team's top options on the depth chart. The Patriots are second in the AFC East with a 5-4 record. They play the Detroit Lions in Week 10 before going on a bye. away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: Star wide receiver A.J. Brown and running back TreVeyon Henderson have already been ruled out for the game. The Patriots might also be missing tight end Hunter Henry, who is still battling the foot injury he suffered in last week's win over the Miami Dolphins. Veteran wide receiver Mack Hollins and interior offensive lineman Greg Van Roten both returned from injured reserve this week to practice. They are officially listed as questionable to play against the Packers. The New England Patriots will once again be shorthanded on the offensive side of the ball when hosting the Green Bay Packers for a visit on Sunday. But it isn't all bad news for the Patriots. Hollins has been one of Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's most reliable downfield targets, and Van Roten was the top replacement at right guard behind Mike Onwenu. Those returns would be a huge lift to a Patriots offense that needs all of the help it can get. home.headline: Patriots vs. Lions Wednesday injury report: AJ Brown returns, three ruled out
home.blurb: Wide receiver A.J. Brown was on hand for it. After missing back-to-back weeks due to a knee issue in addition to the high ankle sprain that sent him to injured reserve in September, the former All-Pro returned as a limited participant to begin Detroit Lions prep. But running back TreVeyon Henderson, offensive lineman Ben Brown and cornerback Carlton Davis III stayed among the sidelined in Foxborough and have officially been ruled out for the matchup in Munich. RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness — out) CB Carlton Davis III (knee — out) An illness that kept Henderson hospitalized for multiple days will now keep the running back out for a third straight game. The Patriots will be without another Brown on offense after the team’s starting left guard exited last Sunday’s 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers with a knee injury. And in the secondary, a knee injury will also keep Davis from taking the field in Munich after he’d worked back from a neck injury throughout October. That leaves four non-participants from Wednesday potentially in play for the NFL international series. FB Reggie Gilliam (knee — IR return) G Greg Van Roten (hamstring — IR return) S Kerby Joseph (knee — PUP return) But a pair of 21-day practice windows are now open for New England along with one 53-man roster spot. After Van Roten headed back to practice last week, Gilliam did so to start work on the Lions. The fullback spent the past five games on injured reserve. He marks the fifth IR return designation utilized by New England. NFL rules allot eight per club. The New England Patriots held practice inside Gillette Stadium on Wednesday before taking an evening flight overseas. Here’s the first injury report ahead of Sunday’s 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff at Allianz Arena. “There’s going to be guys that go to Germany that won’t play,” head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters prior to practice. No. 1 was among seven partial participants for the Patriots on Wednesday. The June trade acquisition hadn’t practiced since late last month and has missed six games altogether amid a season featuring nine receptions for 101 yards. RB Jacob Saylors (neck, hamstring) Under center, Maye continued to be a full participant for New England while carrying a listing due to his right shoulder. The reigning AFC Offensive Player of the Month completed 55 percent of his passes for 299 yards with three touchdowns and three interceptions last weekend. Prior to the blowout loss at home, the quarterback had turned the calendar to November by totaling three scores and only four incompletions in an AFC East comeback against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium.

Meanwhile, safeties Brian Branch (hip) and Kerby Joseph (knee), wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib), and quarterback Jared Goff (chest) were all limited participants. Mahomes didn't end up missing an offensive play in the Chiefs' win, but he did reveal after the game that he'd need further testing on his elbow. According to NFL insider Ian Rapoport, those tests did not reveal a major injury and Mahomes is expected to be good to go for Week 10 against the Atlanta Falcons. The team reportedly will monitor his elbow strain to make sure there is no additional pain or swelling. #Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes underwent an MRI following today’s win and sources say the tests did not reveal a major injury. Kansas City opened as a three-point favorite on the road against the struggling Falcons, but that line has since moved to Chiefs -3.5 at DraftKings Sportsbook . It's not a major change, but it does show that Mahomes should be good to go for Sunday's clash. The Chiefs rebounded from back-to-back losses to crush the Jets, and they're now 6-2 and in the mix to win the AFC West this season. Mahomes (+3000 to win MVP) has thrown for 2,037 yards, 14 scores and just four picks this season while completing over 67 percent of his passes. After missing the end of the 2025 season with a torn ACL, Mahomes has pretty effective in the 2026 season, putting the Chiefs in the mix to win the Super Bowl at +1000. Last season was the first time in the Mahomes era that Kansas City failed to make the playoffs. The Chiefs were expected to be favored in Week 10 -- even on the road -- against the Falcons, and this line could move further if Mahomes is able to practice in full all week. They are each within one half-game of first place in their respective divisions. The Broncos lead Kansas City in the AFC West while the Falcons are looking up at the Panthers and the Saints in the NFC South. This despite Atlanta having lost two in a row and the Chiefs two of their last three. Kansas City is coming off a convincing 35-12 win over the New York Jets, a game that turned after the Chiefs trailed 12-7 in the second quarter. Patrick Mahomes completed 23 of 31 passes for 242 yards and two touchdowns, both scoring passes going to Kenneth Walker III , who was the offensive centerpiece with 102 rushing yards, 143 yards from scrimmage and three total touchdowns. Travis Kelce added 72 receiving yards and even scored on a one-yard run. The defense took over after halftime, holding New York scoreless in the final thirty minutes as the Chiefs pulled away with 21 unanswered second-half points. Kansas City also went 4-for-4 in the red zone, an encouraging development after back-to-back losses to Seattle and Denver. Mahomes did briefly leave the field after hurting his arm/elbow on a strip-sack but returned and finished the game. As a result, the injury report is worth following as gametime approaches. Atlanta, meanwhile, returns home after a disappointing 34-17 loss to Cincinnati in Madrid, its second straight defeat following a 16-0 shutout loss at Tampa Bay. The Falcons opened strongly against the Bengals with an 80-yard drive resulting in a Michael Penix Jr. touchdown pass to Charlie Woerner . The scoring continued as they took a 10-7 lead later in the first quarter, but Cincinnati answered with 17 unanswered points in the second quarter and Atlanta never recovered. Penix finished 20-of-31 for 162 yards, one touchdown and one interception, while Bijan Robinson supplied the offense’s biggest bright spot with 100 rushing yards and a touchdown on 19 carries. Drake London caught five passes for 68 yards, but Atlanta committed 12 penalties for 88 yards and allowed Joe Burrow to throw three touchdown passes. The central storyline from Atlanta’s perspective is will they be able to control the ball and keep Mahomes and co. off the field? The Falcons average 138.8 yards rushing per game. For Kansas City, it is about limiting Bijan Robinson and Atlanta’s rushing attack. The Chiefs have thrived against the run to date this season allowing just 96.3 yards on the ground per game. These teams last met two seasons ago. Mercedes-Benz Stadium was the site and Kansas City won 22-17. Mahomes threw for 217 yards and two touchdowns, while Rashee Rice caught 12 passes for 110 yards and a score; Atlanta, then quarterbacked by Kirk Cousins , had a chance late but could not complete the comeback. The Falcons dropped their second straight game in Week 9, falling to 3-6 at the hands of a pretty fantastic Bengals team. Atlanta’s playoff hopes continue to dwindle, but in the NFC South—where literally every team has 3 wins—they actually aren’t all that low! Unfortunately, things don’t get any easier for the Falcons over the next three games. In Week 10, Atlanta faces the 6-2 Kansas City Chiefs at home, followed by the Vikings and Lions. Atlanta opens as 3.5-point home underdogs against Kansas City, per FanDuel. I’m a little surprised it isn’t higher, to be honest. Sure, the Falcons beat the 49ers a couple weeks back, but that game is looking more and more like a fluke. With the team trading away star safety Jessie Bates III on Monday (and with more potential trades looming), it looks like Atlanta is starting to shift their focus towards the future. The Chiefs, meanwhile, look like a very good team once again. While Kansas City perpetually lacks quality receiving targets, that could change at the trade deadline. They’ve also finally got a quality rushing attack with Kenneth Walker, which is probably the most concerning thing for the Falcons in this one. Atlanta’s defense is very vulnerable to the run and Jeff Ulbrich hasn’t been able to figure out an effective counterpunch. Wide receiver Zachariah Branch did not participate due to a hamstring injury that held him out of Atlanta's last game against Cincinnati; linebacker Josh Woods missed practice due to an ankle injury, and edge rusher James Pearce Jr. was held out with a back injury. Pearce made his season debut against the Bengals but was questionable leading into the game with the same back injury, which was a late development last week. Pearce played 15 snaps as part of Atlanta's defensive line rotation. Linebacker Divine Deablo, who played with his arm wrapped against Cincinnati, was limited on Wednesday. The quarterback was visibly in pain after taking a hit from Jets edge rusher David Bailey late in the first half. The quarterback subsequently underwent an MRI, with the results providing some much-needed encouragement for the franchise. Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) is helped up by guard Trey Smith (65) after being sacked against the New York Jets.Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images Mahomes has now provided another encouraging update on his condition. Speaking about his right elbow on Wednesday, the Chiefs quarterback revealed that he was relieved by the MRI results and believes he is in a good position heading into the Falcons game. "I feel like I'm in a great spot," Mahomes said. "Now, it's just about pain and pain management. I'll do my best to be in the best position possible." (h/t Charles Goldman of A to Z Sports). The MRI revealed no significant damage, with the injury described as an elbow strain or sprain. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid classified Mahomes as day-to-day as Monday, explaining that the quarterback would need rehabilitation to manage the soreness. Mahomes completed 23 of 31 passes for 242 yards and two touchdowns against the Jets despite the injury. Mahomes' latest comments offer encouragement that he is making progress. However, his availability will depend on how his elbow responds as the week progresses. away.headline: Houston Texans safety Reed Blankenship ready to return from broken hand, concussion against Browns
away.blurb: Blankenship, who last suited up against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London last month, returned to practice Wednesday as a limited participant. "You don't really realize how much you love it until you … step back from it for a couple weeks," Blankenship said. "I'm glad I got to spend time with my baby girl too, my wife. But at the end of the day, not going out there and doing what I love for these past couple weeks hurt a little bit." "When I didn't have a kid and a wife, it was different," Blankenship said. "I wanted to stay out there and tough it out, was very stupid. But now start thinking about longevity. You want to be a dad, a father. You wanna be present." Houston Texans safety Reed Blankenship says he's ready to play this weekend versus the Cleveland Browns after missing the past few weeks with a concussion and a broken hand. The Texans signed Blankenship in the offseason to a three-year deal but his start to the season was a rocky one. The lone new player in the Houston starting defense, the unit underperformed in the first few weeks with the secondary in particular taking a step back compared to last year. Despite missing two full games and part of the Jaguars contest, Blankenship is third on the Texans in tackles and one of four players with an interception. Safety M.J. Stewart, who missed the start of the season with an injury of his own, has filled in for Blankenship as the starting safety alongside Calen Bullock. This wasn't Blankenship's first concussion, he said. But his perspective this time around the injury this time is different because of the family and life he is building outside of football. Blankenship said he didn't know when during the Jaguars game he injured his hand. He has a visible scar on the top of his hand, and will probably wear a splint in games. The 27-year-old safety is a right-hander for everything so injuring his left hand would be the preferred option for having a broken hand. But it didn't mean it was easy. "You don't realize how much you need it until it's gone. Well, not gone," Blankenship said to laughs. "You know, gone for a couple weeks." Linebacker Jake Hummel and cornerback Jaylin Smith also returned to practice Wednesday. Hummel has been injured all regular season while Smith got placed on injured reserve after the Week 4 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. Both have a 21-day window to be activated from injured reserve. home.headline: Houston Texans safety Reed Blankenship ready to return from broken hand, concussion against Browns
home.blurb: Blankenship, who last suited up against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London last month, returned to practice Wednesday as a limited participant. "You don't really realize how much you love it until you … step back from it for a couple weeks," Blankenship said. "I'm glad I got to spend time with my baby girl too, my wife. But at the end of the day, not going out there and doing what I love for these past couple weeks hurt a little bit." "When I didn't have a kid and a wife, it was different," Blankenship said. "I wanted to stay out there and tough it out, was very stupid. But now start thinking about longevity. You want to be a dad, a father. You wanna be present." Houston Texans safety Reed Blankenship says he's ready to play this weekend versus the Cleveland Browns after missing the past few weeks with a concussion and a broken hand. The Texans signed Blankenship in the offseason to a three-year deal but his start to the season was a rocky one. The lone new player in the Houston starting defense, the unit underperformed in the first few weeks with the secondary in particular taking a step back compared to last year. Despite missing two full games and part of the Jaguars contest, Blankenship is third on the Texans in tackles and one of four players with an interception. Safety M.J. Stewart, who missed the start of the season with an injury of his own, has filled in for Blankenship as the starting safety alongside Calen Bullock. This wasn't Blankenship's first concussion, he said. But his perspective this time around the injury this time is different because of the family and life he is building outside of football. Blankenship said he didn't know when during the Jaguars game he injured his hand. He has a visible scar on the top of his hand, and will probably wear a splint in games. The 27-year-old safety is a right-hander for everything so injuring his left hand would be the preferred option for having a broken hand. But it didn't mean it was easy. "You don't realize how much you need it until it's gone. Well, not gone," Blankenship said to laughs. "You know, gone for a couple weeks." Linebacker Jake Hummel and cornerback Jaylin Smith also returned to practice Wednesday. Hummel has been injured all regular season while Smith got placed on injured reserve after the Week 4 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. Both have a 21-day window to be activated from injured reserve. David Montgomery didn't practice as he continues to rehab from a groin injury. "David Montgomery is still going through the process," Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said. "He's getting better. Rutledge has started every game this year at left guard after being taken in the first round of the draft. "We'll see how he progresses throughout the week," Ryans said. home.headline: Browns make big Shedeur Sanders announcement for Week 9 amid Deshaun Watson's injury
home.blurb: The Browns will start Sanders, even though Watson has yet to be ruled out for Week 9. He hasn't practiced much this week, and even if he does somehow clear concussion protocol, the Browns will roll with Sanders as the starter for one week. Cleveland could give Sanders the Week 9 and Week 10 start before the team's Week 11 bye, where they could figure out who should be the starting QB for the remainder of the year. But thanks to Deshaun Watson landing in concussion protocol, there is some uncertainty at the quarterback position for this upcoming game against the New Orleans Saints . Todd Monken cleared the air on the QB situation on Friday, as Mary Kat Cabot of Cleveland.com reports that Monken announced Shedeur Sanders will be the team's starting quarterback for Week 9. Shedeur Sanders announced as Week 9 starter for Browns "Browns Shedeur Sanders will start at quarterback vs. the Saints, Todd Monken announced," Cabot reports. With former No. 1 overall pick Kyler Murray set to miss more than just Week 9 with a Grade 2 hamstring strain, the Vikings were desperate to upgrade at quarterback after falling to 6-2. Carson Wentz was awful on Monday night in a loss to the Buffalo Bills, and the Vikings couldn't afford to waste an all-time season from their defense. Cousins' acquisition impacted the Vikings' odds across the betting market. Minnesota went from +2400 to +2200 to win the Super Bowl this season at DraftKings Sportsbook , and it also jumped to -250 to make the playoffs. That's significant, as the Vikings have better playoff odds than the Green Bay Packers, Los Angeles Rams and Seattle Seahawks in the NFC. Now, with Cousins likely in line to play against Green Bay in Week 10, the Vikings are also gaining some ground in the odds for that matchup. Following Monday's loss to Buffalo, DraftKings Sportsbook had moved the Vikings to 4.5-point underdogs on the road after they opened as three-point underdogs on Sunday night. The Packers have won five of their last six games, so this was always going to be a tough matchup on the road, even though the Vikings beat Green Bay in Week 1. Now, with Cousins in the fold, the line has shifted down to Vikings +3.5 at the best betting sites . That's interesting since DraftKings is reporting that just 20 percent of the moneyline bets and 34 percent of the spread bets in this game are on the Vikings. It's pretty shocking that the Vikings are 6-2, and they're hoping Cousins can make a quick adjustment to play in Week 10. After all, Cousins spent multiple seasons in Minnesota and has ran an offense very similar to the Vikings' current scheme at previous stops in his career. That should make it easier for him to start on a short week. This season, Cousins had led the Raiders to a 4-5 start, throwing for 2,340 yards, 20 scores and eight picks. He's not nearly as mobile as he was earlier in his career, but Cousins is certainly an upgrade over Wentz, who was unable to move the Vikings' offense in the loss to Buffalo. The people who set the betting lines, apparently, don't like their chances. Our friends at the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the lines for Sunday's game, and the Vikings currently sit as a 4.5-point underdog to the Packers. The over/under for the game currently rests at 42.5 points. The Vikings, as we all saw on Monday Night Football, appear to have completely abandoned the concept of offense, as they generated none of it in a 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills for their second loss in a row. Carson Wentz stepped in at quarterback for the injured Kyler Murray and turned in what may have been the worst start a Vikings quarterback has put together in recent memory, completing just 8-of-25 passes and turning the ball over three times, including two interceptions. . .a number that could have been significantly higher. The Packers, on the other hand, have won five of their last six after getting off to a 1-2 start. This past week, they absolutely thumped the New England Patriots to the tune of 45-27 behind three more touchdown passes from Jordan Love and a defense that forced Drake Maye into three interceptions. The Packers currently sit in last place in the North, but with a 6-3 record would lead either the NFC South or the NFC East. . .that's just how good the NFC North has been this season. These two teams met in the regular season opener at U.S. Bank Stadium. Wentz came into the game midway through the first quarter after Murray suffered a concussion, and the Packers had a 22-10 lead with just over five minutes remaining in the third quarter. From there, however, the Minnesota defense took over, leading an onslaught against Love and the Green Bay offense that saw the Vikings score 29 unanswered points to finish the game, including forcing a turnover on downs and generating an interception and a fumble to set up scoring opportunities. Minnesota took home the 39-22 win to get their season off to a 1-0 start. With the NFL trade deadline looming at 3:00 PM Central today. . .or approximately seven hours from when this story goes up. . .we will see if anything the Vikings do (or don't do) will shift this number at all. As it stands now, however, the Vikings are currently an underdog to their division rivals as the second half of the season officially gets underway.

That number comes with a little juice at -120, and the Packers are -178 favorites, which comes with an implied probability of 64 percent. If you had said this a few weeks ago, when the Packers' offensive line was drowning, no one would have bought it. Now, after Green Bay finally had a 100-yard rushing performance and beat down on the New England Patriots in all three phases of the game, it looks like the Packers have a real opportunity to make a push for the postseason. The Vikings have played two fewer games than the Packers because: 1) they've already had their bye week and 2) they're playing on Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills. The NFC is so wonky, with the "good" teams being in the North and West, not the South and East, that the 3-6 Tampa Bay Buccaneers currently have about as good a chance of making the playoffs (by winning the NFC South) as do the Los Angeles Rams (a .500 team that is essentially locked into a playoff spot or nothing in 2026), per The Athletic's playoff simulator . In short, there are seven North and West teams fighting for five playoff spots in the NFC, and then there's whatever the hell is happening in the East and South. Do not be surprised at all if a sub-.500 NFC South team ends up hosting a 12-5 (or better record) NFC North team in the wild card round this year.

PFF has him as the Vikings’ highest-graded player and the second-best linebacker in all of football, behind only Jacksonville’s Ventrell Miller. Through eight games, Cashman leads the Vikings in tackles (76), is tied for the team lead in passes defended (7) and tackles for loss (8), and is third in sacks (4.5). He defends the run, gets after the quarterback on blitzes, and drops into coverage all at very high levels. His game against the Colts in Week 7 was one of the best individual games you’ll ever see an off-ball linebacker play. Cashman is also the Vikings’ green dot player, which means he wears a microphone in his helmet and relays the calls from coordinator Brian Flores to his teammates on the field. That responsibility only makes his statistical production even more impressive. The Vikings have a number of players who could take over green-dot duties, including Pace, Wilson, Harrison Smith, and Josh Metellus. Minnesota Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley hinted Kirk Cousins could potentially jump right into the starting lineup beginning with Sunday's matchup at the Green Bay Packers. Teasley told reporters Wednesday it would ultimately be up to head coach Kevin O'Connell to decide which quarterback will start when Kyler Murray is healthy. "I would leave that to Kevin, he's going to put us in the best position to succeed," Teasley said. "But we also didn't acquire Kirk to not play." O'Connell discussed the situation as well: Murray was sidelined with a Grade 2 hamstring strain from Monday's loss to the Buffalo Bills, during which Carson Wentz struggled as his replacement. away.headline: Vikings-Bills Final Injury Report
away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, Kyler Murray is out as expected, as are both Demond Claiborne and Jauan Jennings. Claiborne suffered a knee injury in practice and from Kevin O’Connell’s comments on Saturday, could be out for a while. It wouldn’t be surprising therefore if he was placed on Injured Reserve. It doesn’t appear at the moment that Jennings’ calf injury is a longer-term concern, but we may learn more about that next week. Beyond that, safeties Theo Jackson and Jay Ward are questionable for Monday night. I’m guessing at least one of them will play, but KOC also talked about potentially having Jacob Thomas and/or Tavierre Thomas on the active roster for Monday night to fill in at safety and special teams. For the Bills, backup wide receiver Joshua Palmer is out. But they also have two starting offensive linemen listed as questionable- left tackle Dion Dawkins and left guard Alec Anderson. Dawkins has not practiced all week with a rib injury, so he would seem to be less likely than normal to start with that designation. Anderson was upgraded to limited on Saturday after missing Thursday and Friday practices with an ankle injury. My guess is that if either of them play on Monday night they will be less than 100%, so the left side of the Bills’ offensive line could be a bit more vulnerable than normal. Beyond that, Tyrell Shavers and Jordan Hancock are listed as questionable, but the Bills will need to activate them from the PUP list and IR for them to be eligible to play on Monday night. We’ll see if that happens. home.headline: Kirk Cousins' Status for Vikings vs. Packers Revealed by GM After Raiders Trade at NFL Deadline
home.blurb: For more from Bleacher Report, check out our B/R app , homepage and social feeds—including Twitter , Instagram , Facebook , TikTok and YouTube . Minnesota Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley hinted Kirk Cousins could potentially jump right into the starting lineup beginning with Sunday's matchup at the Green Bay Packers. Teasley told reporters Wednesday it would ultimately be up to head coach Kevin O'Connell to decide which quarterback will start when Kyler Murray is healthy. "I would leave that to Kevin, he's going to put us in the best position to succeed," Teasley said. "But we also didn't acquire Kirk to not play." O'Connell discussed the situation as well: Murray was sidelined with a Grade 2 hamstring strain from Monday's loss to the Buffalo Bills, during which Carson Wentz struggled as his replacement. The Vikings acquired Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders the following day. This article will be updated soon to provide more information and analysis.

home.headline: Injury timeline emerges for Packers RB Josh Jacobs
home.blurb: Packers medical staff tried multiple methods to protect Jacobs’ hand in hopes of getting him back on the field, but he was ultimately unable to return. Jacobs will undergo surgery to repair the issue sometime later this week. According to a report from NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport, he could return to the field for the Packers as quickly as 2-3 weeks. The earliest opportunity for Jacobs’ return is a Week 12 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams. While Jacobs could be back in a couple weeks, there’s also a chance his absence extends for a longer period. If the Packers decide to place him on injured reserve this weekend, he’ll automatically be ruled out for the team’s next four games. If that’s the case, his earliest opportunity to return would be a Week 15 matchup against the Miami Dolphins. Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs fractured his ring finger during the first quarter of this past Sunday’s Week 9 win over the New England Patriots. Green Bay is set for a division-rival matchup against the Minnesota Vikings this coming weekend. After that, the team will enter its Week 11 bye. Jacobs missed the first six games of the Packers’ 2026 campaign on the Commissioner’s Exempt List. The veteran running back recorded three total touchdowns in his two full games back on the field in Weeks 7 and 8. Backup RB Kaleb Johnson stepped up following Jacobs’ exit against the Patriots, rushing for 68 yards and a touchdown on 14 carries. The Packers, led by quarterback Jordan Love, furthered their reputation as one of the best passing offenses in the league. The Packers will kick off against the Vikings at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday. Fans wouldn't be blamed for forgetting that we've got football this coming Sunday after days on end filled with rumors and breaking news at the end of every sentence. Not only do the Titans play in Week 10, but they're hosting AFC South-rivals. The Jacksonville Jaguars, one of the most active buyers at the trade deadline, are coming to Nashville to boast their new pickups. The last time Tennessee faced Jacksonville, the Titans lost 41-7 at the very end of the 2025 season. Cam Ward missed the majority of that game after exiting early with a shoulder injury, and his healthy showing tomorrow is the key to a potential Titans upset. Will: Cam Ward stays hot in Carnell Tate's return Ward nearly led Tennessee to a victory over the (now) 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. The Titans falling short 36-43 in overtime was partly due to Ward taking a costly sack late in regulation, but the QB can't at all be blamed for losing a game he kept Tennessee in. With WR1 Carnell Tate trending toward a return, Ward should have all of his weapons in place to put up another promising game. The Titans even kept RB Tony Pollard at the deadline for Ward's own sake. Again, Jacksonville bulked up at the deadline - their defense specifically - but Tennessee leaving the offense untouched said loud and clear that this franchise believes in Ward. With a newly-gutted defense, the Titans will be relying on Ward to try and secure the win. Won't: Jaguars' overhauled defense clicks immediately Directly opposing Ward is that new-look Jags defense. In addition to adding All-Pro S Jessie Bates III, Jacksonville also acquired defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux. If Tennessee falls short (as is likely expected), it will be because the Jaguars' defense put a stopper in Ward and the offense's growth. That could be one reason among many, but it seems to be the most relevant by far regarding this specific matchup. Prediction: Titans lose, 34-23 At the end of the day on Sunday, I expect Jacksonville will overwhelm Tennessee. I don't believe it will be in blowout fashion, and this is primarily because of the stable flashes of progress Ward showed in Week 8. But between their overhauled defense and Trevor Lawrence manning things under center on offense, the Titans are truly facing a championship contender this week. Perhaps the home field will help blunt the blow, as well as the team debuting their Music City jerseys. I love the jerseys. I like what we saw from Cam Ward in his most recent game. The 6-2 Jaguars are set to travel to Nissan Stadium to face the Tennessee Titans in Week 10, their first game since making blockbuster trades for Jessie Bates and Jordan Davis, along with adding Davon Godchaux for a sixth-round pick. For a Jaguars team that has their eyes set on an AFC South title and a top seed in the playoffs, they are treating the Titans with the same seriousness that they treated the Indianapolis Colts and Baltimore Ravens over the last two weeks. So, how do we see the Jaguars' Week 10 battle with the Titans playing out? We break it down below. Jessie Bates Records An Interception While it certainly remains to be seen if the Jaguars will actually play any of their new defensive pieces against the Titans, I believe they will. Jakobi Meyers and Greg Newsome each played in their first games with the franchise last season after joining the team during that same week, and I think that means we see the trio make their Jaguars debuts. In the process, I think we see Bates create his first Jaguars takeaway right off the bat. Cam Ward is far from the most turnover-prone quarterback the Jaguars have played this season; that distinction goes to Daniel Jones. But he is right near the league average in interception rate, and he has made some egregious decisions with the ball over his last two seasons as a starter. This feels like the perfect week for Anthony Campanile to cook some pressure looks up to confuse Ward, and Bates is a natural playmaker. I think we see his impact right away. Parker Washington Catches 2 TDs The Titans' defense has been ... not very good against slot receivers this season. The Titans rank in the bottom-5 in the NFL against slot targets in each of the following categories: yards per play allowed, yards after the catch allowed, yards after the catch over expectation, and average seperation. The Titans have simply been a mess in the slot, even moving long-time outside cornerback Alontae Taylor to the slot despite signing him in March to play on the outside. As a result, I think this is a Parker Washington week. He is the clear No. 1 receiver in the offense, and I think he shakes off some inconsistent moments we have seen as of late and has a huge game against the Titans. Washington is due for a big performance, and I think we see it this Sunday against the Titans. Cam Ward Throws For Fewer Than 150 Yards There have been 275 quarterback performances this season. In just 39 of those performances, we have seen quarterbacks throw for fewer than 150 yards. Cam Ward makes up two of those games, a number that is trumped only by Bo Nix and Malis Willis which is, well, not great company to be in as far as productive gunslingers go. Ward has been more productive and explosive as of late and is coming off one of the best games of his career, but I predict the Jaguars limit Ward to under 150. Ward threw for just 141 yards against the Jaguars in Week 13 a year ago, and the Jaguars limited Daniel Jones and Joe Fagnano to a combined 189 yards over the last eight quarters. The Jaguars' pass defense is clicking, largely due to the work of defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile, and I believe we see it continue this week. Jaguars Limit Tony Pollard to Under 4.0 YPC Titans running back Tony Pollard has been on a tear over the last few weeks. Pollard, who has rushed for 246 yards and five touchdowns over the last two games, broke out of a mid-season skid and has been able to average over 4.0 yards per carry in every single game but two this season. While Pollard has been one of the NFL's more impressive runners over the last few weeks, I expect the Jaguars to be ready to bottle him up on Sunday. Again, I think the Jaguars will play Davis and Godchaux on Sunday. But even if they don't, I do not think the Titans have the offense to keep the Jaguars off-balance enough to run the ball on them. Teams can only run the ball on the Jaguars when the Jaguars are threatened by the early-down pass, and I do not see the Titans having much success there. Walker Little Pitches Another Shutout The Jaguars have seen Walker Little play really, really well over the last few weeks since stepping into the lineup for an injured Anton Harrison. According to NextGenStats, Little has allowed pressure on just 6.4% of his pass blocks, the fifth lowest rate in the league among left tackles (minimum 100 pass blocks). On his 109 pass blocks, his 87.2% 1-on-1 matchup rate is the highest in the league among left tackles; his 6.3% 1-on-1 pressure rate allowed is the third lowest pressure rate allowed in the league. “The experience always helps. Confidence is a heck of a thing, and I think he's the one that said it in an interview that humility helped. Where obviously he became our swing tackle, and all that guy has done is just stay the course," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said on Wednesday. "Like, never got up, too down. He's just very steady. I really like Walker's play demeanor, the look in his eye recently and not taking everything so seriously. He's able to have fun with it. He's out there playing a game that he loves and competes with, but he's playing at a high level right now. He's got confidence, and you can tell.” Little will mostly draw Titans pass-rusher Jacob Martin, who has had a good year. But after strong showings against the Houston Texans' pass-rush duo in London a month ago and then a dominant outing against Trey Hendrickson last week , I think Little has the edge entering Week 10. He is playing some of the best football of his career right now, and I predict it leads to another shutout. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) head to Nissan Stadium on Sunday in full control of the AFC South for an afternoon game against the last place Tennessee Titans (1-7). The Jaguars have won five of their last six and are coming off consecutive blowout victories. The Titans were off last weekend but take the field having dropped two straight since recording their only victory of the season at Indianapolis back in mid-October. As is the case in most NFL games, the spotlight shines the brightest on the quarterbacks as we approach gameday. Trevor Lawrence is flourishing having thrown for 1,932 yards, 18 touchdowns and only four interceptions. He is an MVP candidate. Tennessee’s Cam Ward continues to labor under center having thrown for 1,483 yards with only six touchdowns and yet five interceptions. His future with Tennessee looks uncertain. Jacksonville’s latest performance was a convincing 33-10 Thursday-night victory at Baltimore, its second straight win by at least 23 points. Lawrence completed 16 of 26 passes for 242 yards and delivered the game’s biggest offensive play, a 50-yard touchdown to Parker Washington late in the second quarter that sent Jacksonville into halftime ahead 17-3. The Jaguars limited Baltimore to 227 total yards, forced three turnovers and kept the Ravens out of the red zone entirely; Baltimore’s only touchdown came on a 65-yard Justice Hill run in the fourth quarter with Jacksonville already leading 33-3. As noted earlier, Tennessee had its bye last week. It came at an ideal time after an exhausting 43-36 overtime loss at Cincinnati, arguably its best offensive showing of the season despite another defeat. The Titans jumped ahead 13-0 and took a 36-29 advantage with just 3:46 remaining when Ward hit Wan’Dale Robinson for a 15-yard touchdown and converted the ensuing two-point try, but Cincinnati tied the game with 1:17 left and won in overtime on Joe Burrow’s nine-yard touchdown run. Ward produced his first career 300-yard passing game, completing 26 of 40 for 304 yards and two touchdowns, while Tony Pollard ran 21 times for 117 yards and two scores. Tennessee accumulated 440 yards and forced four turnovers, including three interceptions by safety Amani Hooker , yet its defense was shredded for 510 yards and allowed Burrow to throw for 462 yards and five touchdowns before his overtime rushing score. The rivalry adds another layer because Jacksonville has emphatically reversed what was once a Tennessee-dominated series. The Titans still lead 35-28 all time, including their famous 33-14 victory over Jacksonville in the 1999 AFC Championship Game, but the Jaguars have won four consecutive meetings and seven of the last 10. Jacksonville swept Tennessee in each of the past two seasons, including a 25-3 win in Nashville last November and a 41-7 rout in Jacksonville on Jan. 4, 2026, the largest Jaguars victory in the history of the rivalry. picks.headline: Titans scouting report vs Jacksonville Jaguars, matchups, prediction NFL Week 10
picks.blurb: News Sports Counties Business Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals TITANS Titans scouting report vs Jacksonville Jaguars, matchups, prediction NFL Week 10 Tyler Palmateer Nashville Tennessean Nov. 11, 2026, 5:02 a.m. CT With a 1-7 record, the Titans' focus for the rest of the season is on player evaluation. The Jacksonville Jaguars lead the AFC South and have strengthened their defense with recent trades. Trading Jeffery Simmons changed everything. The Tennessee Titans quietly submitted to a lost 2026 NFL season by dealing their eighth-year All-Pro defensive tackle to the Chicago Bears on Oct. 29. Tennessee general manager Mike Borgonzi then reinforced the team's desire to build for the future by trading eighth-year veteran safety Amani Hooker to the Buffalo Bills on Nov. 10. Barring a miraculous playoff push without their top two defenders, rivalry points seem to be all that matter for the Titans (1-7) in Week 10 against the Jacksonville Jaguars (6-2) at Nissan Stadium on Nov. 15 (noon CT, FOX). The Titans’ final nine-game stretch will be about observations. Will quarterback Cam Ward play more like a franchise quarterback to finish his second season? Will star rookies Carnell Tate and Anthony Hill Jr. maintain their pace? Who are becoming pieces for Borgonzi’s long-term vision? Finding a way to win one-score games — the Titans have lost six — can help answer those questions regardless of the team’s final record. The Jaguars have won five of their past six games and have a three-game lead in the AFC South. They enhanced their defense this week by trading for All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III from the Atlanta Falcons and 10th-year defensive tackle Davon Godchaux from the New Orleans Saints. Here’s our scouting report for the Titans’ game against the Jaguars. One Jacksonville Jaguars stat to know: 28 That’s career interceptions for Bates. He’ll be a factor. He has at least one interception in each of his nine NFL seasons. Where Tennessee Titans have edge vs. Jaguars Is Ward really the Titans’ only hope? He takes a lot of criticism, some deserved. But why can’t he be an advantage this time? He played at an elite level with a career-high 304 yards passing and two TDs against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. A Ward hot streak in November may be Tennessee’s best chance. The Jaguars rank 21st in the league in passing yards allowed per game (229.0). That’s one spot lower than Cincinnati. There’s an opportunity for Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll to give Ward more downfield throws as he did against the Bengals. Where Jacksonville Jaguars have edge vs. Titans Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence could have a big day against the Titans’ secondary, which was already leaky and now lacks its best player in Hooker. Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals shredded Tennessee with 462 yards passing, three touchdowns and nine plays of 18 yards or more. He was intercepted three times, but all of those came from Hooker. Aside from Alontae Taylor's solid debut at nickel cornerback against the Bengals, other parts of the secondary displayed poor tackling and bad angles. Tennessee ranks 31st in the NFL in passing yards allowed (258.3). Lawrence has thrown for 1,932 yards, 18 touchdowns and four interceptions. He's first in the league with 8.6 yards per pass among active quarterbacks with at least 100 dropbacks, according to Pro Football Focus. Jaguars receiver Parker Washington has 493 yards on 29 catches and is ninth among league receivers with five touchdowns. He ranks third at 17 yards per catch. Matchup to watch Titans defensive end Jacob Martin versus Jaguars left tackle Walker Little. Martin is Tennessee’s best pass rusher with Simmons gone. He had three sacks against the Bengals and has 6.5 for the season. The Jaguars have shuffled their left tackle spot this season. Little has made only three starts, but he didn’t allow a single pressure or sack in last week’s 33-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens. Score prediction: Jaguars 28, Titans 21 Ward and the Titans' offense will maintain their recent progress. But Tennessee's inability to finish games will also continue. away.headline: First injury report of week 10: Dolphins offense could be even more short-handed against Indianapolis
away.blurb: The Dolphins released their first injury report of Week 10 on Wednesday and what stood out was center Aaron Brewer not practice because of a concussion. While it's too early to rule out Brewer for the game against the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium, the fact he didn't practice Wednesday doesn't bode well. Based on the Return to Play protocol for players dealing with concussions, it's probably a must that Brewer practice Thursday on a limited basis for him to have a chance to play against the Colts. Robinson had to sit out the Week 2 game against San Francisco, while Proctor missed the Week 8 game against the New England Patriots. It should be noted that ahead of that New England game, cornerback JuJu Brents also missed the Wednesday practice because of a concussion before he was limited Thursday and a full participant Friday. He ended up playing against the Patriots. The other issue to monitor on offense involves rookie wide receiver Chris Bell, who is back on the injury report with limited participation in practice because of a knee issue. Quarterback Kyle McCord is set to make his NFL debut for the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, but it might have to do without having the team's All-Pro center snapping him the ball. And rest assured the Dolphins will be very careful not to rush him into action. The Dolphins unfortunately are becoming accustomed to having to deal with concussions, as both edge defender Chop Robinson and guard Kadyn Proctor missed a game this season because of that issue. Brewer played every snap against the Lions during the 19-9 loss Sunday, so this llikely was another case of him reporting symptoms the following day. The other player on the 53-man roster who didn't practice Wednesday was rookie tight end Will Kacmarek, who is dealing with quad/knee issues. He left the game against Detroit after taking a big shot to the side of the leg after a short reception and was seen at practice Wednesday wearing a compression sleeve on his left leg. If he were unable to play against Indianapolis, it likely would mean more reps for fellow rookie Seydou Traore, who's gotten more involved on offense is recent weeks and also would mean an appearance by waiver wire pick-up Justin Joly. Bell, who is nearing the one-year anniversary of the torn ACL he sustained in his final season at Louisville, last was on the injury report before the Week 5 game against the Cincinnati Bengals. It's logical to think, though not certain, he's dealing with some soreness in his surgically repaired knee. That obviously isn't a great development after he wasn't on the injury report at all for the past three games. Bell played 36 offensive snaps against Detroit after playing 45 against the New England Patriots. He was targeted only once against the Lions, the result being an incomplete pass.
