home.headline: Dolphins add QB Malik Willis to IR due to lingering groin injury; Kyle McCord expected to start vs. Colts
home.blurb: Dolphins add QB Malik Willis to IR due to lingering groin injury; Kyle McCord expected to start vs. Colts - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Cam Schlittler, Jacob Misiorowski win AL and NL Cy Young Awards TRENDING NFL news, live updates Ridley on airport 'incident' Teddy Ricketson Contributing writer Tue, November 10, 2026 at 9:27 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Miami Dolphins announced Tuesday that they are placing quarterback Malik Willis on injured reserve . Willis has had a lingering groin injury that has been impacting his mobility. The quarterback had an MRI, and it showed that it is now a core muscle injury. Willis doesn't need surgery, but the amount of rest required to recover necessitated an IR stint. With Willis sidelined for at least the next month, backup quarterback Kyle McCord is expected to take over as the starter this weekend against the Indianapolis Colts, per ESPN's Adam Schefter . Willis is not expected to miss the remainder of the season. Willis joined the Dolphins this offseason, signing a 3-year, $67.5 million deal in free agency. He reunited with new Miami head coach Jeff Hafley, who was with Willis last year in Green Bay as the defensive coordinator. Willis has played in eight games this season and has thrown for 1,396 yards, 6 touchdowns and 6 interceptions. The 27-year-old is known for being able to use his legs and has picked up 232 yards and three additional scores on the ground. Willis is currently Miami's second-leading rusher behind Ollie Gordon (463 yards, 4 TDs). McCord was a sixth-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft by the Philadelphia Eagles. He spent the season on Philadelphia's practice squad, but joined the Packers in the offseason on a reserve/futures contract. The quarterback was then traded to the Dolphins in late August for a 2028 sixth-round pick to replace Quinn Ewers, whom Miami traded to the Jacksonville Jaguars. McCord has yet to play a snap in his pro career, but that is expected to change Sunday against the Colts, as he is in line to make his first career start. The 6-foot-1, 210-pound Jackson led the league in passes defended in 2025 while playing alongside Jaycee Horn, who notched his second consecutive Pro Bowl a year ago. This season, Jackson has recorded six tackles; he had surgery very soon after the game at Cleveland on Sept. 27. Jackson has been out since after Week 3 with a groin injury. He exited the same game as Horn did — both starting corners went on the injured reserve at the same tim e — and has since seen his defensive backfield deteriorate under the stress of injury. Against the Denver Broncos last week, the Panthers played the contest without their top four corners: Horn, Jackson, rookie Will Lee and Akayleb Evans. "One man's storm is another man's paradise," Jackson said at the time of his injury. "I'm going through a storm. But for these guys, it's paradise, because they're about to get an (opportunity). I'm telling them to take full advantage of it. To be honest, this is how this league works. It's next man up. (Akayleb) or Will can go out there and get two picks, and now it's like, 'Do we ride with him? What happens when Mike Jack comes back?' "Just getting in and out of my brakes," he said. "Film study. Because teams are still gonna try to attack us. Now that we're playing a lot of post-high, we're going to get a lot of Cover 3 beaters: all four verts, things like that. So now that we understand those beaters, it's all about going out and making the play." home.blurb: The New Orleans Saints plan to activate the rookie wide receiver off injured reserve for Sunday’s game against the Cleveland Browns, according to a report. Tyson, the eighth overall pick in this year’s draft, has been out since getting hurt Aug. 13 with a hamstring injury and missed the Saints’ first seven games, but he returned to practice this week. Tyson’s return should help a Saints offense that has been uneven this season. The Saints rank 14th in points per game, but 23rd in total offense. Most of the team’s struggles have centered around the run game — the Saints fired run game coordinator T.J. Paganetti on Monday — but Tyson provides another dynamic weapon in the passing game, which could help open up New Orleans’ rushing attack. The Saints had previously listed Tyson as questionable. Though draft analysts were concerned about the receiver’s durability due to Tyson’s injury history in college, the Saints were confident that Tyson would be able to hold up in the NFL. home.headline: Travis Etienne Jr.'s Practice Return Creates Murky Fantasy Football Situation in the New Orleans Saints' Backfield
home.blurb: The Saints Backfield Shuffle: What Travis Etienne’s Impending Return Means for Fantasy Football Managers Now, with the Saints opening his 21-day practice window, the team will "see how the week plays out" before determining if he is ready to suit up for a crucial divisional clash. While Etienne's return is a welcome boost for a New Orleans offense looking to secure the NFC South crown, it introduces a major headache for fantasy managers holding shares of Alvin Kamara and breakout waiver wire darling Audric Estime. However, managers should temper expectations for his immediate return. Hamstring injuries are notoriously tricky for running backs, and Kellen Moore's cautious tone suggests they may ease him back into the rotation (if he even plays against the Carolina Panthers this week). Etienne's impending return is bad news for fantasy managers planning on relying on Alvin Kamara or Audric Estime down the stretch. During Etienne's lengthy five-game absence, the Saints' backfield morphed into a shifting puzzle. Alvin Kamara has continued to command a steady role, but his efficiency and volume have fluctuated. An active Etienne directly eats into his touches, explosive play opportunities, and red-zone looks that anchor Kamara’s weekly floor. While Kamara’s skill set keeps him relevant, his path to anything more than risky flex numbers narrows significantly once Etienne assumes his starting workload. Audric Estime is even more vulnerable. He capitalized on the depleted depth chart to carve out an expanded role and became a popular waiver-wire pickup this week, but a healthy Etienne completely caps Estime’s fantasy football utility. Without an outright injury ahead of him on the depth chart, Estime projects to slide back into a game-script-dependent rotational role, making him difficult to trust in most leagues. If you roster Travis Etienne, hold tight and make sure he is stashed safely in your active or IR spot as he nears a game-day designation. If you are relying on Alvin Kamara, prepare for a hit to his weekly ceiling as touches are redistributed. As for Audric Estime managers, it might be time to treat him strictly as a high-end handcuff. The Saints are still very much in the NFC South playoff hunt, and how this three-way backfield shakes out as part of their playoff push will dictate fantasy championships across the board. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Buffalo Bills (7-1) visit the New York Jets (2-7) on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium, with the AFC East rivals heading in dramatically different directions. Buffalo sits three games clear of second-place New England atop the division while the Jets have lost four in a row and sit but a half-game out of the cellar in the AFC East. The Bills enter the week with the NFL’s highest-scoring offense at 32.0 points per game and lead the league with 386.4 yards per game, powered by Josh Allen and a rushing attack featuring James Cook III . The Jets, meanwhile, are averaging just 20.2 points per game which begs the question: Can Geno Smith and the Jets score enough to keep up with the Bills’ elite attack? Working in the Jets’ favor is that Buffalo has a short turnaround after grinding out a 23-6 road victory over the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night. It was a far more physical game than the final score suggests. The Bills managed just three points on their first six possessions, and Allen threw an early interception, but his 25-yard touchdown pass to Keleki Latu with 44 seconds remaining in the first half gave Buffalo a 10-6 advantage. From there the Bills wore down Minnesota, holding the ball for an extraordinary 42:32 and running 79 offensive plays. Cook carried 31 times for 107 yards, including a five-yard fourth-quarter touchdown, while Allen finished 21-of-31 for 234 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Buffalo’s defense was even better, limiting Minnesota to 178 total yards and nine first downs while forcing three turnovers. The Jets return home after a 35-12 loss at Kansas City. Despite an early 6-0 lead, New York’s offensive woes were impossible to ignore. Smith and co. repeatedly stalled and had to settle for four Jason Sanders field goals. The Chiefs led just 14-12 at halftime before completely controlling the second half. New York finished with only 229 yards, went 2-for-12 on third down and failed to score a touchdown, while Smith completed 18 of 32 passes for 165 yards and was sacked five times. Breece Hall returned from a five-game absence caused by a quadriceps injury and produced 87 yards from scrimmage, while rookie Omar Cooper Jr. led the Jets with eight catches for 58 yards. Recent history adds another challenge for New York. Buffalo has won eight of the past 10 meetings, including a couple smacks last season, beating the Jets 30-10 at MetLife Stadium on Sept. 14, 2025 and 35-8 in Buffalo on Jan. 4, 2026. away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, Kyler Murray being out is the big news and he will not play on Monday night. Theo Jackson also did not practice on Thursday and seems more questionable whether he'll play or not. Kevin O'Connell said they have other safeties like Jay Ward who could play in Jackson's absence and a few others are possbilities to be active on Monday night if need be as well. The rest of the injuries appear to be more of the 'playing through it' variety and don't seem like they'll keep those players out on Monday night. And while he was able to return as a full practice participant ahead of the Week 8 loss to Denver, the Chiefs still had Kelce listed on the injury report with the same ankle issue. Kelce has also remained on the injury report heading into the Week 9 matchup against the Jets. He was initially listed as a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, but the Chiefs upgraded him to a full participant on Thursday, easing concerns about the tight end's status for gameday. Like Kelce, wide receivers Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) and Nikko Remegio (hip) were also limited on Wednesday, but were upgraded to full participants on Thursday as well. "Chiefs injury report for Thursday is out," The Kansas City Star's Pete Sweeney wrote on X. "Travis Kelce (ankle), Nikko Remigio (hip) and Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) have been upgraded to FULL participants. Mansoor Delane (shoulder) and Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) remain LIMITED." But despite playing in every game at age 37, so far, Kelce has found himself on the injury report over the last few weeks. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Seattle Seahawks (5-4) head to Las Vegas on Sunday trying to establish some momentum in a tightly packed NFC West race, while the Raiders (4-5) are looking to rebound from one of their sloppiest performances of the season AND are looking to do so with rookie Fernando Mendoza making his first start of his career. The matchup is a monster challenge for Mendoza: Seattle has leaned on a defense allowing just 18.0 points per game, tied for fourth-best in the league entering the week, while Las Vegas has surrendered 29.8 per game, ranking last. So you expect the Raiders would look to lean on Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington Jr. to run the ball and take the pressure off their rookie signal-caller…but know that the Seahawks allow an average of 89.1 yards per game (151.2 for the Raiders). Quarterback is also a storyline for the Seahawks. Sam Darnold remains sidelined with a quad injury after also reportedly cracking a rib against Chicago, while Drew Lock came out of this past Sunday’s game dealing with an oblique issue after previously battling elbow tendinitis. Seattle comes in off a much-needed 17-3 victory over Arizona, a game it controlled despite playing without starting quarterback Darnold. Backup Lock completed 19 of 28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown, while tight end AJ Barner supplied both Seattle touchdowns, catching one from Lock and running for another. Zach Charbonnet , recently returned from an ACL injury, gave the offense some balance with 77 yards on 16 carries, and the defense held Arizona to 216 total yards and no touchdowns. Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught seven passes for 51 yards and became the first NFL receiver to reach 1,000 yards this season. Las Vegas, meanwhile, is trying to clean up the turnovers after a 38-17 loss at San Francisco dropped it below .500. The Raiders were actually within 21-10 at halftime, but Kirk Cousins was intercepted on the first play of the third quarter and Jaden Dugger returned it 35 yards for a touchdown, beginning a disastrous second half. Cousins finished 22-of-32 for 216 yards, one touchdown and three interceptions as Las Vegas committed five turnovers, managed only 240 total yards and 24 rushing yards, and possessed the ball for just 21:42. Brock Bowers was possibly the only bright spot, catching seven passes for 111 yards and a touchdown. Sunday’s game is also a reunion of two franchises with considerably more history than their present-day conference alignment suggests. The Raiders and Seahawks were AFC West rivals from 1977 through 2001, and the Raiders lead the overall series 30-26, including postseason games. Seahawks vs. Raiders Week 10 predictions: Jaxon Smith-Njigba First TD odds as Klint Kubiak faces his old offense
picks.blurb: Seahawks vs. Raiders Week 10 predictions: Jaxon Smith-Njigba First TD odds as Klint Kubiak faces his old offense - oregonlive.com Skip to Article Set weather Back To Main Menu Close Weather in - Change Location Current - Mostly Sunny Tonight Low - Mostly Sunny Tomorrow High - Mostly Sunny Full Weather Report Sports Betting Published: Nov. 11, 2026, 9:15 a.m. Sina Torki | Special Correspondent Klint Kubiak called the plays for Seattle’s Super Bowl offense last season. On Sunday he sees that offense from the other sideline. Kubiak’s Las Vegas Raiders (4-5) host the Seahawks (5-4) at Allegiant Stadium, and the betting market has spent the week moving toward his team. DraftKings opened Seattle as a 7-point favorite, according to ESPN . Bet365 now has the Seahawks at -3.5. Seattle comes in off a 17-3 home win over Arizona. Las Vegas lost 38-17 at San Francisco. The records and recent form favor the Seahawks, but the line movement says the market thinks this is much closer to a field-goal game than it first looked. Jaxon Smith-Njigba is again the shortest price to score first, though at a longer number than he was against the Cardinals. Teams: Seattle Seahawks at Las Vegas Raiders Date: Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026 Kickoff: 1:05 p.m. PT (4:05 p.m. ET) Location: Allegiant Stadium, Las Vegas TV: CBS ( Seahawks viewing guide ) Records: Seahawks 5-4, Raiders 4-5 More: NFL.com game center · NFL standings · NFL injury reports Seahawks vs. Raiders odds Odds are from Bet365 and are accurate at time of publication. Spread: Seahawks -3.5 (-105), Raiders +3.5 (-115) Moneyline: Seahawks -182, Raiders +152 Total: Over 43.5 (-105), Under 43.5 (-115) The moneyline implies roughly 64.5% for Seattle. The spread and total together point to a final around Seahawks 23.5, Raiders 20. Las Vegas is the more expensive side of the spread at -115, a sign the market still sees value in the hook even after three and a half points of movement. Jaxon Smith-Njigba to score the first touchdown (+425) Bet365 has Smith-Njigba at +425 to open the scoring , an implied probability of roughly 19.0%. His -130 anytime price implies roughly 56.5%. He was +350 to score first against Arizona last week, so the market has lengthened him in a game it expects to be closer and played on the road. He leads Seattle with 1,036 receiving yards and nine touchdowns, per NFL.com , and is the only player on this board priced shorter than even money to score at any point. The gap to the rest of the board is narrower than last week. Zach Charbonnet is +600 to score first (roughly 14.3%) and Brock Bowers is +625 (roughly 13.8%), both about five points behind. On the anytime market, Charbonnet and Bowers are both +115 (roughly 46.5%), 10 points back. Bowers is the case against. The Raiders score 26.4 points per game, eighth in the league, four more than Seattle’s 22.4. Kirk Cousins has 20 touchdown passes, and Bowers has six touchdown catches as his top target. The board makes Seattle more likely to score first, with the visible Seahawks (Smith-Njigba, Charbonnet and Jadarian Price) at roughly 44.4% against 33.2% for the visible Raiders (Bowers, Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington Jr.), before the sportsbook’s margin. But Las Vegas has been the better scoring team this season, and Bowers at +625 gets you most of Smith-Njigba’s chance at a better price. If you think Kubiak’s knowledge of Seattle’s defense gives the Raiders an edge early, Bowers is the alternative to Smith-Njigba. First and anytime touchdown scorer odds Jaxon Smith-Njigba Zach Charbonnet Jadarian Price Ashton Jeanty Mike Washington Jr. Jeanty’s +800 is long for a back drafted sixth overall a year ago. NFL.com lists him at 362 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown this season, which goes a long way toward explaining the price. Washington’s presence on the board points to a Las Vegas backfield that is more of a split than Jeanty’s draft position suggested. Kirk Cousins passing yards Bet365’s passing yardage ladder has Cousins at -165 to reach 225 yards (roughly 62.3%) and +115 to reach 250 (roughly 46.5%). His last five games came in at 243, 313, 295, 247 and 216. He cleared 225 in four of them and 250 in two. Las Vegas ranks 30th in time of possession, so its drives tend to be short and pass-heavy, and that supports the 225 line. Same Game Parlays on the board Bet365’s featured Same Game Parlays for this game: Four Score (+1900, $10 pays $200): Zach Charbonnet, Ashton Jeanty, Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Brock Bowers each to score a TD End Zone Encore (+2800, $10 pays $290): Jadarian Price, Mike Washington Jr. and Cooper Kupp each to score a TD Four Score takes the top two names from each side and needs a game with plenty of touchdowns, which sits awkwardly with a 43.5 total. End Zone Encore is the long-shot version built from secondary options. Kupp doesn’t appear among the six visible names on the touchdown scorer board. Seahawks vs. Raiders prediction and best bet A spread that moves from 7 to 3.5 usually means one of two things: new injury information or a market that decided the opener was wrong. Either way, the value on the Raiders side has mostly been taken. At +3.5 for -115, Las Vegas needs to cover about 53.5% of the time, and it has gone 1-4 in its last five. The total looks more interesting. The market has 43.5 points, and the Under is the more expensive side. The season numbers point the other way. Las Vegas averages 26.4 points and Seattle 22.4, and Cousins has passed for more than 240 yards in four of his last five games. The Raiders rank 30th in time of possession, so their drives are short, which tends to give both offenses more possessions. Kubiak also knows Seattle’s personnel from last season, and that should help Las Vegas’s offense more than its defense. The counterargument is Seattle’s defense, which ranks fourth in interceptions, and a Seahawks offense that sits 17th in yards per game. If Seattle controls the clock and Cousins throws into coverage, this can stay in the low 40s. Even so, the scoring averages and the quarterback numbers support the Over more than the Under. Best bet: Over 43.5 (-105) at Bet365 For the prop, Smith-Njigba at +425 is a better price than last week for the same role. If you would rather not need him to open the scoring, his -130 anytime price at Bet365 is the steadier route. Lock was limited in practice on Wednesday, with head coach Mike Macdonald indicating that the veteran is "making good progress" and may start against the Raiders. Whoever is under center will once again be working with a patchwork offensive line as stars Quenton Nelson and Charles Cross did not practice. Nelson is battling a knee injury that might hold him out for his second straight game while Cross has been out with an ankle injury since Week 7. Backup guard Anthony Bradford continues to be hampered by a knee injury and was limited on Wednesday. On the defensive side, Leonard Williams remains out with a stinger that he suffered against the Kansas City Chiefs, and edge rusher Derick Hall was limited with a new back injury. away.headline: ‘They Didn’t Have To Tell Us That,’ ‘Definitely Unusual’ — NFL Analyst Questions Seahawks’ Decision To Reveal Sam Darnold’s Surprise Injury
away.blurb: The Seattle Seahawks will be without Sam Darnold for their Week 9 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, but the timing of the team’s announcement seems questionable to some, especially given its decision to disclose the quarterback’s injuries. “So they got a lot of faith in Drew Lock. I just think that this idea that Wednesday, out of the blue, they tell us that Sam Darnold is out with a quad injury. They tell us that he’s week to week, which usually means you’re going to miss a couple of weeks. They didn’t have to tell us that,” Florio said. “Now I appreciate the transparency, because what they could have done, they could have just put him down as did not practice. They could have done that yesterday. They could have done it today. They could have done it tomorrow, and then they could have called him out on Friday,” the analyst continued. Drew Lock is expected to start against Arizona, although his availability for Seattle is not settled. The veteran is managing a right-elbow injury and was listed as limited on Wednesday’s estimated injury report after Seattle held a walkthrough. Darnold, meanwhile, is considered week-to-week and has not been placed on injured reserve. The cracked rib could potentially be managed while playing, but the quad injury is expected to keep him out against Arizona. Coach Mike Macdonald confirmed Wednesday that Darnold would miss Sunday’s game because of a quad injury suffered late in Seattle’s 34-17 loss to the Chicago Bears. Mike Florio Questions Seahawks’ Decision To Announce Sam Darnold’s Absence Early While the coach disclosed the injury, Macdonald also revealed that the quarterback had played through a cracked rib for nearly the entire game. Darnold suffered the injury on the second play against Chicago after taking a hard hit from blitzing cornerback Kyler Gordon. He did not report the issue to the coaching or medical staff during the game and continued playing through the final whistle. He finished with two touchdown passes despite the injury, and Seattle’s coaches and medical staff did not learn about the cracked rib until after the game. The decision to reveal the extent of Darnold’s injuries, however, prompted NFL analyst Mike Florio to question why Seattle chose to announce the quarterback’s absence on Wednesday rather than wait until later in the week. Speaking on “NFL on NBC” with Chris Simms, Florio said the Seahawks could have followed the league’s injury reporting rules without immediately confirming that Darnold would miss Sunday’s game. “But they decided to just lead with their chin on this, which I thought was strange. It’s definitely unusual, and it forfeits the uncertainty that the Cardinals would have as to who they’re getting ready for. Now they know they’re getting ready for Drew Lock or Jalen Milroe,” Florio added. away.headline: Rams-Cardinals injury report: McDuffie, Curl and Ferguson DNP Wednesday
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: To start the week, the Rams listed 10 players on their initial injury report, five of whom did not practice at all. The Rams only held a walk-through, so participation is an estimate. Trent McDuffie, Kam Curl and Terrance Ferguson were all non-participants. Sean McVay said the Rams are "optimistic" McDuffie will be able to play on Sunday, which is a good sign despite his absence Wednesday. Curl played last week after being questionable with a foot injury, but he's now listed with a toe injury. Ferguson is dealing with a hamstring injury after pulling it in practice last week. He's still on IR but can be activated at any time. Colby Parkinson continues to battle a rib injury, but it's encouraging that he was at least limited on Wednesday. Joe Cardona could be making progress with his ankle injury, too. Myles Garrett continues to nurse his knee injury and Davis Allen has an oblique injury that forced him to be limited. On the Cardinals' injury report, Budda Baker had a rest day, and Hjalte Froholdt missed practice while recovering from a concussion. Bam Knight is still progressing through the concussion protocol and was limited in practice. Josh Sweat and Isaac Seumalo both got veteran rest days, too. This article originally appeared on Rams Wire: Rams-Cardinals injury report: McDuffie, Curl and Ferguson DNP Wednesday After two days of unfortunate injury news and trade speculation, the Los Angeles Rams are back at work on Wednesday. They have one game left before their bye, as they'll visit the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday in an attempt to avenge their shocking Week 6 loss to their division rival. The Rams still haven't overcome the injuries suffered in that game, remaining without Davante Adams, Kobie Turner and Poona Ford, but the Cardinals are in much worse shape. They're without Jeremiyah Love and now Michael Wilson, while Jacoby Brissett has been traded and his replacement, Gardner Minshew, is injured, too. Puka Nacua and Steve Avila were obviously non-participants; they will each miss multiple weeks. Click the post above to see the full report for Arizona.

away.headline: New NFL Trade Rumors on Rams' Ladd McConkey Pursuit Amid Puka Nacua, Davante Adams Injuries
away.blurb: Fowler added the Rams ultimately "didn't seriously consider a receiver move" because the team expects Matthew Stafford to succeed in the short term before Nacua and Adams return later this season. Adams has not played since rupturing his hamstring Oct. 18. Fowler reported at the time Adams hoped to return "as close to the post-Week 11 bye as possible." The Rams have also yet a few weeks to determine the future of Terrance Ferguson, who suffered a hamstring strain during his 21-day return-to-practice window on his way to coming back from an ankle injury. He must return by the end of that three-week stretch or sit out the rest of the season. The Rams have a Sunday road game against the Arizona Cardinals coming up before sitting out a Week 11 bye. McVay will hope a wide receiver room currently led by Tutu Atwell and Konata Mumpfield can keep this team afloat until Adams and Nacua are able to return in what his team hopes will be the near future. Justin Herbert reportedly wasn't the only player about whom the winless Los Angeles Chargers rebuffed trade inquiries ahead of Tuesday's deadline. The Los Angeles Rams are believed to have asked after wide receiver Ladd McConkey following the injuries that have sidelined Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday. "The Chargers said no to at least one Ladd McConkey inquiry," Fowler reported. "Teams I spoke to believe the Rams were the ones to make that call." Rams to Consider Trade After Puka Injury The news comes after NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported the Minnesota Vikings expressed interest in trading for Herbert before the Chargers "immediately shut down all inquiries." McConkey, who is under contract through 2027, has gone from serving as Herbert's top target last season to recording just 17 catches with 286 yards and a touchdown in six games with the struggling Chargers' offense. He missed his second game of the season last Sunday after suffering back spasms ahead of kickoff against the Houston Texans. The Rams still might have hoped a fresh start for McConkey would help the wide receiver would help add some depth around Stafford in a campaign during which he has yet to play up to his 2025 MVP form. Nacua could be hoping for a similar timeline given that the wide receiver has not yet been placed on injured reserve, although Rams coach Sean McVay has said the team expects to lose him for at least a month with an MCL and PCL sprain as well as turf toe in his right leg. home.headline: Cardinals QB situation takes stunning turn with Gardner Minshew update: Report
home.blurb: Following their 17-3 road loss Sunday to the Seattle Seahawks, the Arizona Cardinals received a major update on quarterback Gardner Minshew, who may have suffered a season-ending injury. On Monday evening, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that Minshew “is feared to have suffered a torn UCL in his throwing arm.” Rapoport said Minshew suffered the injury before halftime but continued playing through it. According to Rapoport, Minshew will get additional testing done, but the injury could end his season and require a lengthy rehabilitation process. Minshew suffered the injury when he was hit by Seahawks pass rusher Dante Fowler while attempting a pass on the final play of the first half. The Cardinals quarterback grabbed his right arm after the rough hit, but continued to play. In Sunday’s game, Minshew completed 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards and was sacked three times by the Seahawks defense. Seattle held Arizona to just 198 total yards of offense for the game. More news: Chiefs HC Andy Reid Reveals Patrick Mahomes Injury Update Ahead of Falcons Game The devastating update arrived days after the team traded veteran starter Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens. Arizona’s unfortunate situation with Minshew has led to several developments, including Adam Schefter reporting that the team signed Josh Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals’ practice squad. This is Johnson’s 15th team in 14 seasons. According to ESPN , in an initial report on the Cardinals’ injury updates, rookie Carson Beck was expected to start on Sunday. The Cardinals drafted the former Miami Hurricanes quarterback at No. 65 in the 3rd round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Beck led his team to the College Football Playoff National Championship game, which they lost to Fernando Mendoza and the Indiana Hoosiers. The decision to draft Beck was met with mixed reviews, with many sports outlets giving the team a low grade for the pick. NFL.com’s Chad Reuter graded Arizona’s Day 2 picks, including Beck, an “A,” indicating he had “a lot of big-game experience.” However, Reuter also noted that Beck’s decision-making was too inconsistent to be a “surefire starter.” Beck appeared in the NFL Hall of Fame Game this preseason against the Carolina Panthers, throwing for 188 yards and a touchdown in Arizona’s 33-30 loss. With ESPN reporting that Beck is expected to start Sunday, he’s poised to take over for a 3-6 Arizona team, unless they opt to use Johnson instead. Unfortunately, both quarterbacks could face a challenging matchup for the team’s next NFL game. The Cardinals host a Los Angeles Rams team on Sunday, Nov. 15, that has now won three straight games to improve to 5-4 for the season. The Rams also just got back the NFL Defensive Player of the Year, Myles Garrett, who recorded three sacks on Sunday in their 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders, so Beck or Johnson could face a difficult test for his first NFL start. home.headline: Just how bad are Cardinals injuries? See where they rank
home.blurb: To be fair, the Cardinals’ injuries are largely limited to the offensive side of the ball. Cornerback Will Johnson is out for the season with a neck injury, but he is the only defensive starter currently sidelined. And yet, he’s never seen an injury crisis quite like the one he faces in his debut season as the Arizona Cardinals head coach. “Not to this level, no,” LaFleur said. “At least in one particular position group.” So, just how bad are the Cardinals' injuries? Well, just look at their Week 1 offensive depth chart: RB: Jeremiyah Love (injured reserve) WR: Michael Wilson (injured reserve) WR: Marvin Harrison Jr. (traded) WR: Kendrick Bourne (injured reserve) LT: Paris Johnson Jr. (injured reserve) C: Hjalte Froholdt (concussion protocol) If Froholdt indeed misses this week’s game, the Cardinals would be down to just four of their Week 1 starters. Even excluding him, they’ve lost six of those top 11. The results tell the story. Over the past four weeks, the Cardinals rank a respectable 19th in points per drive allowed and 12th in yards per play allowed. It’s been their best defensive stretch in nearly two years. On the flip side, their offense ranks 24th and 28th, respectively, in those same metrics. “The defense, there's been a guy here and there, but there's been some decent continuity over the last month,” LaFleur said. “And I think you guys see that. I think you see 11 as one more and more each week, particularly over these last four weeks. Not the case on offense right now.” It’s an injury barrage that is unmatched across the league. The Cardinals’ seven offensive players on injured reserve is the most in the league, with those four aforementioned Week 1 starters joined by Gardner Minshew, Jalen Brooks and Hunter Long. Only one other team — the Los Angeles Chargers — even has six offensive players on IR. League average is 2.7. When looking only at offensive starters, the story is similar, as the Cardinals lead the league with four on IR. Only two teams — the New England Patriots and Los Angeles Rams — have three offensive starters on IR. League average is 1.2. The Cardinals’ defense, by contrast, has had slightly better health than league average. Still, just 43 of the 53 players from the Cardinals’ Week 1 squad remain on the active roster. Only the Atlanta Falcons have had more attrition. As a result, it’s difficult to assess exactly where the Cardinals roster stands. That’s not to say that their poor performances have been entirely attributable to injury — Marvin Harrison Jr., the offensive line and the pass rush have all struggled even when healthy. But any overarching assessment, at least on offense, has to account for the unwelcome wave of injuries.

Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton At one time…a few decades ago…the 49ers and the Cowboys was the top rivalry in the NFL. In 2026, Sunday’s game between the 49ers (7-1) and the Cowboys (4-5) features one team contending for a Super Bowl and the other simply battling to remain in contention in an underwhelming division. The contrast extends beyond the standings is explained in the numbers: the 49ers are averaging 29.4 points per game while allowing 19.5, compared with 27.3 scored and 26.2 allowed by the Cowboys. San Francisco arrives in Arlington following a convincing 38-17 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders, a game the 49ers broke open with a turnover-fueled second half. Brock Purdy completed 17 of 25 passes for 232 yards and two touchdowns and also ran for a score, while Christian McCaffrey scored once on the ground and once through the air. San Francisco led 21-10 at halftime before Jaden Dugger returned an interception 35 yards for a touchdown on the Raiders’ first offensive play of the third quarter. That started a remarkable half in which the 49ers forced five turnovers. The Niners finished with 414 total yards, including 190 rushing, possessed the ball for more than 38 minutes. Dallas also enters the matchup following a victory, escaping Indianapolis with a 27-23 win over the Colts after trailing 23-20 with less than two minutes remaining. Dak Prescott immediately answered with a 46-yard completion to Ryan Flournoy , and Javonte Williams scored from one yard out with 1:08 remaining to put Dallas ahead for good. The Cowboys piled up 508 yards of offense to Indianapolis’ 271, with Prescott completing 21 of 34 passes for 335 yards and two touchdowns, CeeDee Lamb exploding for 10 catches and 195 yards and a score, and Williams rushing for 101 yards. But Dallas made life difficult for itself with two turnovers and 14 penalties for 153 yards. This is a rivalry that has produced some of the most memorable postseason games in NFL history, from “The Catch” in the 1981 NFC Championship Game to three consecutive NFC title-game meetings between the clubs following the 1992, 1993 and 1994 seasons. San Francisco currently owns the upper hand, leading the all-time series 21-19-1 and having won the past four meetings, including playoff victories of 23-17 after the 2021 season and 19-12 after the 2022 season. The 49ers followed those wins with a 42-10 rout in 2023 and a 30-24 victory in the most recent meeting on Oct. 27, 2024. home.headline: Cowboys injury report: Overshown’s latest setback, Pickens and Porter Jr. updates
home.blurb: But the Cowboys won't be going into this game fully staffed either. Earlier this week, fans learned that Malachi Lawrence would be out for several weeks with an ankle injury, but he's not the only one in danger of missing this weekend's contest. Let's check out the latest regarding DeMarvion Overshown, George Pickens, Joey Porter Jr., Caleb Downs and others. On Friday, Schotteheimer told 105.3 The Fan that they needed to "get him out there today and see how he does.” Overshown is questionable after being limited the last two days. It always seems to be something with him, unfortunately, so fans won't hold their breath for Overshown to be active. Pickens has been dealing with a multitude of injuries this year, it seems, which at least partially explains his downturn in production. He was limited in all three practices leading up to the Colts game, and he is also questionable for Sunday. Dallas knew Porter Jr. was not 100% upon his arrival, but he's been a mainstay on the injury report and a full-on question mark every week, it feels like. He was full on Wednesday but has been limited the last two days, which is a bit worrisome, but Porter Jr. is questionable for Week 9. Schottenheimer said before Friday's practice that he was "hopeful" to have both Pickens and Porter Jr. against Indianapolis. Fans will find out Sunday morning if that was just wishful thinking. After missing the last two-plus games, Dee Winters will return for Dallas. The Cowboys have not had a fully healthy linebacker corps for an entire game this season, and if Overshown misses Sunday, it will remain that way. But for the time being, he is at least insurance if Overshown is out. Jake Ferguson improved from a non-participant on Wednesday and Thursday to being limited on Friday. It remains to be seen if he can play through his ankle injury, but he is officially questionable. Of course, Malachi Lawrence is out with the aforementioned ankle injury, and Kavontae Turpin will miss his third straight game with an injury to his ribs. Jonathan Bullard and Marist Liufau have not been activated to the 53-man roster, but they both practiced in full all week. Officially, they are questionable as the Cowboys mull over their roster math equations. Rapid fire: Luke Schoonmaker is questionable. Tyler Smith and Kenny Clark are good to go. The Dallas Cowboys' season already feels like it is on the ropes in Week 9 as they travel to take on one of the only teams in the NFL that are spiraling worse than they are: the Indianapolis Colts. And this is a get-right game if I've ever seen one, or if that even matters for Brian Schottenheimer's team. Indianapolis has already sold off great veterans like Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, and word on the street is that Josh Downs and Jonathan Taylor, and maybe more, could be next. Pittsburgh got the best of Cincy in the first meeting between these teams, winning 30-27 at home, giving it the current tiebreaker in the division. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers had one of his best games of the season, throwing for 292 yards, three scores and one pick to lead the Steelers to a win at home. Now, they find themselves as underdogs on the road out of their bye week agaist Joe Burrow and Co. The Bengals are on fire right now, knocking off the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid in Week 9 for their fourth win in a row. Burrow, who is now tied with Josh Allen in the odds to win the MVP award this season, has thrown 16 scores over the last four weeks and adding a rushing touchdown for good measure in the blowout win over Atlanta. Oddsmakers have given the Bengals the edge in this division, setting them as odds-on favorites to win it ahead of this Week 10 clash. Pittsburgh won the division in the 2025 season, and with the Baltimore Ravens and Cleveland Browns both losing in Week 9, this is shaping up to be a two-team race. So, all of those games look to be pretty bankable. “Whereas the Steelers really have a much rougher path. They've still got to play the [Denver] Broncos and the Jags (Jacksonville Jaguars). Their only real bankable wins are the [Tennessee] Titans, and then they get two Ravens games.” It'll be interesting to see if this line moves at all in the coming days, but it appears the Bengals are going to close as favorites as they look to split the season series with their AFC North rival. picks.headline: ‘Bring your popcorn’- Mike Tomlin makes bold prediction for Steelers-Bengals clash
picks.blurb: ‘Bring your popcorn’- Mike Tomlin makes bold prediction for Steelers-Bengals clash - Yahoo Sports Search query for Search Search News Finance More Mail NFL Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images Aryan Chadha · HITC Mon, 9 November 2026 at 11:30 am UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Premier League Scottish Football Champions League Europa League Club World Cup About our ads Mike Tomlin is expecting a blockbuster AFC North showdown between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals, backing both teams to deliver an entertaining contest with the division lead at stake. The former Steelers head coach knows exactly what this rivalry means after spending 19 years in Pittsburgh before stepping away from the role. He will now get to watch his old team from the NBC crew as the two sides prepare to meet on Sunday Night Football. Both teams enter the contest with 6-2 records and four consecutive victories, setting up a major meeting between two sides looking to strengthen their position in the AFC North. Mike Tomlin backs Steelers pass rush to challenge Joe Burrow and Cincinnati Bengals Tomlin made no secret of his excitement when discussing the matchup, admitting he would be more than happy to make the trip to Cincinnati. "It's AFC North football and you know I love that. You can airmail me right to Cincinnati," Tomlin said. He also highlighted the individual battle that could define the game, with Joe Burrow and the Bengals passing attack facing Pittsburgh's formidable pass rush. "It's good on good. Joe Burrow and that Cincinnati passing game vs T.J. Watt and the four-man rush of the Steelers…. Bring your popcorn and get your cameras ready." Pittsburgh will arrive with plenty of confidence after enjoying a bye week. The Steelers' four-game winning run includes a commanding 27-6 victory over the Cleveland Browns in their most recent outing. Cincinnati have also found their rhythm, beating the Atlanta Falcons 34-17 in Madrid. Burrow completed 82.8 per cent of his passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in that victory. However, the Bengals will have revenge on their minds after losing 30-27 to Pittsburgh during their earlier meeting this season. That defeat came during a difficult spell in which Cincinnati also suffered a second consecutive loss. Now, with both teams level at 6-2, the stakes are considerably higher. picks.blurb: Bengals vs. Steelers predictions: Joe Burrow, Jaylen Warren and a 34-31 final - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football Cam Schlittler, Jacob Misiorowski win AL and NL Cy Young Awards TRENDING NFL news, live updates NFL midseason awards Rex Ryan arrested Ridley on airport 'incident' CFP committee gets it right Bengals vs. Steelers predictions: Joe Burrow, Jaylen Warren and a 34-31 final (Sam Greene/The Enquirer / USA TODAY) Keegan Nickoson · Roundtable Sports Wed, November 11, 2026 at 11:53 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Joe Burrow accounts for four touchdowns for the fifth straight game Burrow is on a heater, scoring four or more touchdowns, whether throwing or running, in four straight games. In his last four games against the Steelers, Burrow has thrown 11 touchdowns and four interceptions, topping 275 yards in all four games. Interestingly, Pittsburgh is a great matchup for Burrow. The Steelers play zone coverage on 84.3% of dropbacks, according to Next Gen Stats, and Burrow is the best quarterback in the NFL against zone by completion percentage, at 74.7%. Jaylen Warren rushes for 120-plus yards Warren has become one of the league's most productive running backs this season, ranking sixth in rushing yards and first in yards per carry, at 5.9. Earlier this season against the Bengals , Warren ran for the second-most yards of his season, with 127. Two weeks ago against Cleveland, Warren topped that number with 143 yards. It was the first time all season he rushed for 100 yards in back-to-back games. The Bengals' defense has been inconsistent this season, struggling with tackling some weeks and shutting down opposing offenses and forcing takeaways in others. I think that, coming off a bye, the Steelers catch the Bengals on their back foot and feed Warren, who will have a big game. Steelers win 34-31 History is not on the Bengals' side in this matchup. After playing an overseas game, teams are 0-5 when their next game comes against a team coming off a bye. The Steelers are rested, while the Bengals are recovering from nearly a full week in Madrid. A lot is at stake in this game, with the winner taking sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Pittsburgh doesn't have much momentum, especially on offense, as its best wide receiver, DK Metcalf, has been struggling with drops lately. He has just 378 receiving yards this season and has topped 100 yards just once, with a 115-yard day against Cleveland earlier this season. Metcalf had just one catch for 4 yards on six targets against the Browns. The Steelers hit a snag at the right time, giving themselves a week to figure things out. I think the Steelers pick up a big win, halting the Bengals' momentum and getting a massive tiebreaker. Pittsburgh has done a relatively good job of keeping a cap on Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins over the last couple of seasons. Outside of Chase's massive 16-catch, 161-yard game with Joe Flacco at quarterback last season, neither has topped 100 yards in their last four meetings.

away.headline: Pittsburgh Steelers fans might be disappointed, but Mike McCarthy isn’t worried about missing the trade deadline
away.blurb: Pittsburgh Steelers fans might be disappointed, but Mike McCarthy isn’t worried about missing the trade deadline - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Cam Schlittler, Jacob Misiorowski win AL and NL Cy Young Awards TRENDING NFL news, live updates Ridley on airport 'incident' Nick Farabaugh · PennLive.com Wed, November 11, 2026 at 9:19 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers did not end up making any big moves at the trade deadline, and that was not much of a surprise. With the team standing pat, however, head coach Mike McCarthy says he is happy with his wide receiver room. If the Steelers were going to trade for a player, it likely would have been at the wide receiver position. "I feel great about our guys. I mean, we're getting guys healthy. Michael [Pittman Jr.] is getting close, obviously, Roman [Wilson] and Max [Hurleman]. So, we've got good young guys. Both the Brandons [Smith and Johnson]. So, we've got a group that I'm excited to continue to work with," McCarthy said. McCarthy was not as involved in the decision-making process for trades as general manager Omar Khan. In the past, head coach Mike Tomlin had been heavily involved in the decisions being made on the roster. While McCarthy certainly has a say in those, it seems he is not as active as some other coaches in that area of team building. "I think my individual focus is always on our current roster. I spoke on this, was it yesterday? When was the last time we talked? I think it's important, as I've learned over the years, to keep the energy there. I mean, I understand what goes on. I mean, that's what Omar [Khan] and our personnel staff is always working on, player acquisition and grading of players and that whole process.So, as far as what all went down, that's probably better-served for questions for others. I'm focused on our guys," McCarthy said. The Steelers made some additions to their roster in the post trade deadline craze a year ago. They signed Adam Thielen and Marquez Valdes-Scantling at wide receiver and brought in Asante Samuel Jr. at cornerback. Pittsburgh could still make some of those moves on the margins this year, but if they do make those types of moves, they are unlikely to be as impactful as a potential trade could have been for the team. home.blurb: The Bengals returned to practice today as the roster works through the lingering jet lag from last week's trip to Spain. Cincinnati is pretty healthy coming out of the first half of the season, and the latest injury report largely reflected that. He was officially limited in the Bengals' injury report. They went through a walkthrough on Wednesday afternoon. DJ Turner was also limited due to an ankle issue. Jonathan Allen (rest) and Kyle Dugger (quad) didn't participate. Check out the full report below, which included a handful of Steelers players. Check out the full Wednesday injury report below: Dylan Fairchild was the only new addition to the injury report after he got dinged right at the end of Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons. Cincinnati had some veteran rest days mixed in to start the week but should have a pretty full-strength roster to attack the Steelers with on Sunday night. They are fresh off a great bonding experience in Spain. "It seemed like they spent a lot of time together outside the hotel," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said about the trip. "My favorite part of winning a game like that and long travel is the plane. Just the volume on the plane, the camaraderie on the plane. That's generally when you know it's been a good day, good trip, and I certainly felt that last night. "I'm sitting in my seat, and I'm watching all the players come by and the attitude they have, and they're joking with their teammates and telling stories about the week or telling stories about the game. That is probably my favorite part of any of the road experiences." Getting as healthy as possible will help Cincinnati take control of the AFC North. Losing both games to the Steelers this season would make it even more difficult to win the AFC North. Names on injured reserve like Andrei Iosivas (thumb), cornerback Ja'Sir Taylor (hamstring), and rookie offensive lineman Brian Parker (knee) are eligible to come off injured reserve but its unlear if they will get activated this week. On top of the jet lag, Cincinnati has to overcome a Pittsburgh team fresh off of its bye week. "I don't know what the stats are. I just know they're not great. I honestly can't even give you a ballpark of what they are," Taylor said about no international game team ever beating an opponent fresh off a bye the following week. "I just think common sense would tell you it's probably a little challenging. But I think we have a great mindset right now." home.headline: Zac Taylor Shares Encouraging Injury Updates on Several Bengals Players
home.blurb: Zac Taylor confirmed on Wednesday that starting left guard Dylan Fairchild is day-to-day after suffering an apparent shoulder injury during the waning moments of the Bengals' victory over the Falcons. Fairchild appeared to suffer the injury just before the two-minute warning in Madrid and attempted to finish the game afterwards, though he tapped out immediately afterwards. Taylor also shared an update on rookie pass rusher Cashius Howell, refusing to rule Howell out for the season and instead labeling him week-to-week. The Bengals placed him on injured reserve after he sustained a wrist injury that required surgery in Week 8 against the Titans. He is eligible to return from IR after the team's Week 12 game against the Saints on 11/29, though Taylor said Howell will miss time beyond that. Several Players Could Return from Injured Reserve This Week Taylor also updated the media on the possible return of several key players from injured reserve this week, leaving the door open for names such as Andrei Iosivas to return to the active roster. Rumors have surfaced that Iosivas could return soon after having thumb surgery earlier in the season. He is the most likely candidate for a return from injured reserve at the moment, with names such as Jalen Davis, Ja'Sir Taylor, and Brian Parker II also getting close to a possible return. The return of either Davis or Taylor would provide a solid boost to a corner room that is missing any sort of stability at nickel corner, as Dax Hill and Josh Newton have filled that role since Davis' injury. As for Parker, his return may happen at the perfect time. If Fairchild misses any time, Jacob Bayer would likely slot into the left guard spot with Parker also in the mix. away.headline: Justin Herbert Injured, DJ Uiagalelei Makes NFL Debut as Chargers Fall to 0-8 in Loss to Texans
away.blurb: "Could be a fracture, we'll find out," Harbaugh told reporters after the game on Sunday. The Chargers quarterback, who went undrafted out of Florida State, came in for Herbert late in the fourth quarter as his team trailed big. The prospect of Uiagalelei taking the starting job from Herbert would have sounded like a joke coming into the season, but nothing is out of the realm of possibility amid an 0-8 start. Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert avoided a fractured finger after suffering an injury during Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Houston Texans, coach Jim Harbaugh revealed on Monday. Harbaugh said on Sunday that Herbert wanted to finish the game, but the coaching staff thought better of it. Herbert said he will do "whatever I can to make sure I'm 100 percent." While Harbaugh noted Herbert wanted to play through the injury, the coach opted to have DJ Uiagalelei—who made his NFL debut on Sunday—finish the game. Uiagalelei's first drive ended with a touchdown pass. Uiagalelei finished his first NFL game with 24 yards and a touchdown on 2-of-7 passing. It had been another rough day for Herbert before he exited, as he had just 193 yards, a touchdown and an interception. Herbert came into the game with 1,398 passing yards, five touchdowns and 10 interceptions. Before Sunday, he hadn't thrown a touchdown pass since Week 5. The Chargers' hopes of reaching the playoffs are essentially over at this point, but bringing in a new starting quarterback could give the team a spark heading into the second half of the season. Uiagalelei had a five-year college career with Clemson, Oregon State and Florida State, though he never quite lived up to the hype he had coming into college. After going undrafted in 2025, he signed with the Chargers but didn't make the 53-man roster. He spent last season on the team's practice squad. Over the offseason, he competed for the backup position behind Herbert but ultimately lost to Trey Lance and started the year on the practice squad. After Lance was placed on the injured reserve with a groin injury in September, Uiagalelei was promoted to the active roster, paving the way for him to serve as Herbert's backup.

November 10, 2026 / 4:51 PM EST / CBS Baltimore The Baltimore Ravens are in need of a kicker after the Atlanta Falcons reportedly poached Jake Moody from their practice squad on Tuesday. Moody is signing with the Falcons and will be added to their 53-man roster, according to NFL insider Jordan Schultz . Moody was elevated to the Ravens' active roster ahead of their 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Nov. 5, making a 53-yard field goal in the game. Moody joined the Ravens' practice squad twice this season as the team looked for competition for struggling kicker Tyler Loop. Loop was placed on injured reserve with a groin injury and will miss at least the next three games. He has converted 13 of 17 field goal attempts this season, including just two of five attempts from 40 to 49 yards. However, Loop has also made kicks from 57 and 64 yards, with the latter securing a win over the Dallas Cowboys in Brazil. Moody rejoined Baltimore's practice squad on Oct. 19 and appeared in one game for the Ravens. Now, the Ravens (4-5), who sit in last place in the AFC North, must find another kicker and add him to their 53-man roster before their next game against the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football, Nov. 16.

If Brissett starts Monday night against the Los Angeles Chargers, he will be the Ravens' fourth starting quarterback this season. Players told WBAL-TV 11 Sports that any time someone gets traded, it provides a spark in the locker room. But really, what Brissett brings that the team desperately needed was continuity at the quarterback position. Brissett is a journeyman of sorts, having played on seven different organizations throughout his 11 years in the NFL. Through those stops, he gained something valuable: Experience. “He's a vet. He's been here a long time. He's been in about every system, played with a lot of guys. He knows what looks right and what looks wrong,” Ravens center Cam Jurgens said. “Honestly, I'm just excited to see his leadership, his communication, how he talks with the guys.” One of the things that make Brissett unique is his versatility as he has played in many different systems under various head coaches, which allows him to be adaptable to any system. “It's great. I remember I played against him and the (Cleveland) Browns when we were at home. He's a great quarterback, a very savvy vet. So, he's someone who brings in a lot of experience and I'm excited, everybody is,” Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike said. That experience is already being shared with the younger quarterbacks on the team. “He's won a lot of games in this league, has been in some great quarterback rooms and he's a great quarterback himself. So, that's how I'm looking at it. It'll be a great opportunity to learn from him and see how he learns the game and how he prepares,” Ravens rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano said. This season, Brissett has started eight games for the Arizona Cardinals, throwing for more than 1,700 yards and 10 touchdowns with seven interceptions. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said he has already seen the ways Brissett can will contribute to the Ravens. “High level, high experience, leader in the locker room, leader in the walk-throughs, leader in the meeting room, not afraid to speak up and say, ‘Hey, I like this. home.headline: Lamar Jackson's Message to Ravens Revealed in NFL Rumors amid Injury, Return Buzz and Losing Streak
home.blurb: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is aiming to return during the 2026 NFL season, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport . After playing the first three games of the year, he missed three games because of a high ankle sprain, returning to action on Nov. 1 against the Buffalo Bills. His return was brief, however, as he suffered a thumb injury on the Ravens' first offensive drive. Rapoport reported that Jackson spoke to the team and delivered an "energizing" and "exciting" message. The overall theme was to "just stay alive" until he's healthy enough to be back on the field. The Ravens are last in the AFC North at 4-5 following Thursday's 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. The combined absences of Jackson and Tyler Huntley were glaring as third-stringer Joe Fagnano threw for 60 yards and two interceptions on 18 attempts. Jackson has unfortunately had another injury-riddled year. The injury required surgery, and the two-time MVP was placed on the injured reserve immediately after the game. Huntley came in for Jackson after his injury, but he was forced to exit soon after because of a turf toe injury. A day after the Jaguars loss, Baltimore acquired Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals. Brissett is a significant upgrade from Fagnano and may be enough for the team to keep its head above water in the weeks ahead. It's clear Jackson isn't throwing away the rest of the season, and that attitude is bound to spread to the rest of the locker room.

home.blurb: While it doesn't feel like there's much to be hopeful about as it pertains to the Charm City franchise, the face of it isn't ready to throw in the towel just yet. According to a report from NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , star quarterback Lamar Jackson told his teammates that he plans to return this season, with the hope of leading them on a late-season push for the postseason. After starting the season winning four of their first five games, the Ravens now sit at 4-5 and currently sit outside of the current playoff picture at the bottom of the AFC North division standings. With eight games and a bye week remaining on their schedule, in order to return to the postseason after just falling short last year, they'll need to start stacking some wins. The earliest Jackson is eligible to return is Week 14, when the Ravens host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, following the team's Week 13 bye. That will be five weeks post-op and at the earliest possible end of the spectrum for his potential return. If the Ravens can rattle off four straight wins or at least go 2-2 over that span, they'll be in a great position to make Jackson's push to return worthwhile. It'd be just in time for their final four games, all of which are against AFC North rivals, including a pair of bouts with the current division-leading Pittsburgh Steelers. Moody rejoined Baltimore's practice squad on Oct. 19 and appeared in one game for the Ravens. Now, the Ravens (4-5), who sit in last place in the AFC North, must find another kicker and add him to their 53-man roster before their next game against the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football, Nov. 16.

home.blurb: Baltimore is working out a group of free-agent kickers Wednesday, including Riley Patterson and Harrison Mevis, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. The auditions come as Tyler Loop is on injured reserve and the Ravens prepare to host the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football. Moody handled Baltimore’s kicking duties during Thursday’s 33-10 loss to Jacksonville, connecting on a 53-yard field goal and his only extra-point attempt. Atlanta subsequently signed him from the Ravens’ practice squad, leaving Baltimore needing another replacement before its next game. Loop opened this season as Baltimore’s kicker before a right groin injury landed him on injured reserve Nov. 3. Moody provided an experienced alternative, but his departure means the Ravens must prepare another specialist while Loop remains unavailable. A new kicker will not solve Baltimore’s broader offensive problems, but converting available scoring opportunities remains essential. Wednesday’s workouts are the next step toward filling a vacancy the Ravens briefly appeared to have addressed with Moody. Facebook-f Twitter Instagram Youtube Home The Clay Travis and Buck Sexton Show Brian Kroneberger Morning Money Report The Closing Bell – Akers Financial Traffic Baltimore Traffic Conditions By Samantha Croston, WBAL-TV 11 The Baltimore Ravens returned to practice Wednesday with a new quarterback in veteran Jacoby Brissett . If Brissett starts Monday night against the Los Angeles Chargers, he will be the Ravens' fourth starting quarterback this season. Players told WBAL-TV 11 Sports that any time someone gets traded, it provides a spark in the locker room. But really, what Brissett brings that the team desperately needed was continuity at the quarterback position. Brissett is a journeyman of sorts, having played on seven different organizations throughout his 11 years in the NFL. Through those stops, he gained something valuable: Experience. “He's a vet. He's been here a long time. He's been in about every system, played with a lot of guys. He knows what looks right and what looks wrong,” Ravens center Cam Jurgens said. “Honestly, I'm just excited to see his leadership, his communication, how he talks with the guys.” One of the things that make Brissett unique is his versatility as he has played in many different systems under various head coaches, which allows him to be adaptable to any system. “It's great. I remember I played against him and the (Cleveland) Browns when we were at home. He's a great quarterback, a very savvy vet. So, he's someone who brings in a lot of experience and I'm excited, everybody is,” Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike said. That experience is already being shared with the younger quarterbacks on the team. “He's won a lot of games in this league, has been in some great quarterback rooms and he's a great quarterback himself. So, that's how I'm looking at it. It'll be a great opportunity to learn from him and see how he learns the game and how he prepares,” Ravens rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano said. This season, Brissett has started eight games for the Arizona Cardinals, throwing for more than 1,700 yards and 10 touchdowns with seven interceptions. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said he has already seen the ways Brissett can will contribute to the Ravens. “High level, high experience, leader in the locker room, leader in the walk-throughs, leader in the meeting room, not afraid to speak up and say, ‘Hey, I like this. I like that. Hey, you need to do this, make sure we're on the same page here,'&#822
